title: Young Economist Program
raw_text: MINECOFIN/BNR Young Economist Program with GIZ support 9th Cohort – 2026/2027 Background The Young Economist Program (YEP) provides an excellent opportunity for aspiring young Rwandan economists and helps create a strong “recruitment pool” of highly qualified Economists who can take up professional and leadership positions in the Ministry of Finance and Economic Planning (MINECOFIN), the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR), and other government ministries and agencies. The program seeks to bridge the gap between academia, the workplace, and policy analysis, while equipping young economists with a strong understanding of the role of public policy in sustainably improving the well-being of the population. The program is implemented by MINECOFIN and BNR with the support of GIZ Rwanda. Since 2016, eight cohorts have graduated, contributing to a growing pool of young economists serving across key public institutions, including MINECOFIN, BNR, the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA), and the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR). Notably, approximately 90% of staff in MINECOFIN’s Office of the Chief Economist are graduates of the previous eight cohorts. The program is now preparing for its ninth cohort. The YEP combines practical experience with structured learning and mentorship. Participants gain hands-on experience at MINECOFIN and BNR, benefit from mentorship and seminars delivered by national and international experts, complete relevant online and in-person courses, and prepare and present analytical briefs. Their professional conduct and performance are assessed throughout the program. The program targets highly qualified Rwandan economists aged 30 years or below who hold at least a bachelor’s degree in Economics, Development Economics, Macro-Fiscal Economics, International Trade/Economics, Monetary Economics, Econometrics, Statistics, or a related field. A master’s degree in one of these fields is considered an asset. About the YEP 9 The 2026/27 YEP equips Young Professionals with the skills and experience required to work across different economic departments of MINECOFIN and other ministries and government agencies. The program combines three main components: (a) a continuous internship with on-the-job training and mentoring; (b) intermittent formal group training in applied economics, quantitative methods, and relevant software/s; and (c) continuous self-study, including a research project at a later stage of the program. Progress and performance are assessed throughout the program through performance evaluations and written tests. Learning outcomes By the end of the program, participants are expected to have strengthened their competencies in three core areas: Applied economic analysis and problem-solving: Critically assess economic and policy issues and apply economic concepts and analytical approaches to policy questions arising in the day-to-day work of MINECOFIN and other public Economic institutions. Quantitative and data analysis: Apply quantitative methods and relevant software/s for macroeconomic projections, policy analysis, and assessing the impacts of policies and external developments on the economy and citizens’ well-being. Communication and collaboration: Clearly communicate analytical findings and policy recommendations to different audiences, engage effectively with peers and supervisors, and contribute constructively to teamwork and institutional building. Location: Kigali, Rwanda Fixed Term: 6 months renewable once Positions: 20 Level: Trainees A. Responsibilities As part of the YEP training, participants will be assigned to MINECOFIN, BNR, and, where applicable, other government ministries and agencies for supervised on-the-job learning. During these assignments, participants will undertake the following training-related responsibilities: Young Economist – Key Responsibilities Conduct applied economic and policy analysis to support evidence-based decision-making, and policy formulation. Collect, manage, and analyze economic data using appropriate statistical, econometric, and quantitative methods and tools, including Excel, E-views, and STATA. Support macroeconomic monitoring, projection, and forecasting by analyzing key economic indicators, emerging trends, and development across the national economy. Analyze real, fiscal, monetary, external, and financial sectors developments and their implications for the economy. Apply macroeconomic and econometric models to assess policy options, economic scenarios, and effects of shocks on economic performance. Prepare analytical briefs, reports, and presentations to communicate economic findings to technical teams and policymakers. Support feasibility studies, project appraisal, economic and financial analysis, Cost-Benefit Analysis, and the implementation and follow-up of government programs and projects. Collaborate with government and development partners on economic research, policy analysis, and capacity-building activities. Participate in on-the-job learning, mentoring, teamwork, and continuous professional development, while undertaking assignments and receiving guidance and feedback from supervisors and mentors. B. Required qualifications, competences and experience. Qualifications Have an “A0” (3–4-year undergraduate) or master’s degree in one or a combination of the following: Economics, Development Economics, Macro-fiscal Economics, International Trade/Economics, Monetary Economics, Econometrics, Statistics. Comprehend public policy, and the relevance of economic analysis for public policy making affecting levels of living (poverty), environmental quality, and the distribution of access to health/education and economic opportunity. Be fluent in Kinyarwanda and English; knowledge of French is an advantage. Rwandan Nationals aged 30 years or below Practical Skills Proven research and (quantitative and qualitative) data analytical skills; Thorough understanding of Economic Models, Descriptive Statistics, Econometrics & Regression Analysis; Knowledge of Excel, Econometrics, Modelling, data management software/s; Proven solid English report writing skills; Ability to communicate well, work in teams, and prioritize tasks under deadlines. How to Apply Interested candidate should submit their application no later than October 23, 2026, at 5:00 PM. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application. Note: All attachments should be put together in one PDF file, not larger than 2 MB. Incomplete or late submissions (missing certain files) will result in automatic disqualification. An individual may participate in the Young Economist Program (YEP) only once. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for test and interviews. Apply

Editorial Voice and Written Communications Own the development and implementation of LEAP's engagement and communications strategy, working closely with LEAP Leadership and the LEAP Program Manager. title: Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat
raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE EXECUTIVE COORDINATOR - ACE-AJ SECRETARIAT Position Executive Coordinator, ACE-AJ Secretariat Host institution Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda Scope Pan-African / multi-country Reporting ACE-AJ Founding Members, through the governance and hosting arrangements of ACE-AJ and LAF Duty station Kigali,Rwanda,withregularregionaland international engagement Contract Full-time; terms to be specified in the employment contract 1. Institutional Background and Rationale The African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice (ACE-AJ) is a Pan-African platform established to strengthen access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights and people-centred justice across Africa. Its origins lie in a continentally grounded feasibility process undertaken in 2016 through consultations with access-to-justice organisations in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Rwanda, Malawi and South Africa. The feasibility work examined the relevance, scope, sustainability, institutional form and operational requirements of a continental centre and identified the need for a stronger African voice, systematic knowledge exchange, research, learning, capacity development and collaboration among organisations working closest to communities. The feasibility process envisaged the Centre as more than a conventional project or secretariat. It was conceived as a galvanising space for access-to-justice and legal-empowerment actors; a repository of African practice and evidence; a platform for peer learning and exchange; a mechanism for strengthening community-based justice; and a vehicle through which African organisations could develop collective positions and speak with greater coherence on continental and global justice questions. ACE-AJ was officially launched in Kigali, Rwanda, in 2017. Since its establishment, it has evolved into a multi-country network bringing together civil society organisations and justice actors committed to expanding access to justice for poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities. The Legal Aid Forum (LAF), Rwanda, is a founding member and hosts the ACE-AJ Secretariat. ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 provides the current institutional roadmap. It organises the Centre’s work around five mutually reinforcing priorities: promoting holistic justice delivery; strengthening capacity building; research and knowledge generation; advocacy and communication; and strengthening the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The Strategy also places substantial emphasis on monitoring, learning, institutional visibility, membership growth, strategic partnerships and diversified resource mobilisation. 2. Purpose and Strategic Character of the Position The Executive Coordinator is the principal executive and operational lead of the ACE-AJ Secretariat. The purpose of the position is to provide disciplined continental coordination and executive leadership for the implementation of ACE-AJ’s Constitution, Strategic Framework 2024–2030, decisions of the General Assembly and Board, approved programmes and institutional commitments. The Executive Coordinator will move ACE-AJ from strategy to implementation. The office holder will connect a geographically dispersed membership, translate strategic priorities into annual and multi-year plans, mobilise resources, coordinate multi-country programmes, strengthen governance and institutional systems, generate and communicate evidence, develop strategic partnerships and position ACE-AJ as a credible African platform on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. The position therefore requires a network builder and institutional entrepreneur, not only a programme administrator. The Executive Coordinator must combine continental vision with implementation discipline; diplomacy with accountability; strong member relations with external representation; and programme leadership with fundraising, knowledge generation and organisational development. 3. Overall Accountability Serve as the principal executive focal point for implementation of ACE-AJ’s Strategic Framework 2024–2030 and approved annual priorities. Ensure that decisions of the General Assembly and Board are translated into clear workstreams, responsibilities, timelines, budgets, deliverables and measurable results. Lead the day-to-day work of the Secretariat and coordinate Secretariat personnel, consultants, technical advisers and designated support from member organisations. Maintain effective operational coordination with LAF as host institution while safeguarding ACE-AJ’s distinct continental identity, governance and member ownership. Provide timely, evidence-based advice to the Board on institutional development, programme performance, partnerships, funding, risks and emerging access-to-justice trends. 4. Key Responsibilities 4.1 Continental Network Coordination, Membership and Movement Building Provide proactive day-to-day coordination of ACE-AJ as a Pan-African network and maintain substantive engagement with members across countries, regions, legal traditions and languages. Develop an annual member-engagement architecture covering consultations, focal-person meetings, peer exchanges, communities of practice, thematic working groups, institutional visits and regional or continental convenings. Maintain structured two-way communication between the Secretariat, Board, General Assembly, founding members, and strategic partners. Map and continuously update member expertise, innovations, community-justice models, research, policy experience, institutional capacities and support needs. Strengthen member ownership by creating practical opportunities for members to lead research, training, advocacy, convening and cross-country initiatives. Lead strategic membership growth, with particular attention to geographic balance and stronger representation from underrepresented parts of the continent. Coordinate membership admission, onboarding, orientation, retention and an accurate, functional membership database. Identify common challenges across jurisdictions and convert them into collective learning, research, advocacy and programme initiatives. 4.2 Strategy Implementation and Institutional Performance Translate the 2024–2030 Strategic Framework into costed annual work plans, implementation matrices, institutional calendars and measurable performance commitments. Coordinate implementation across all five strategic priorities and ensure that programme choices remain connected to ACE-AJ’s mission, comparative advantage and member experience. Develop a Secretariat performance dashboard showing progress against strategic outcomes, programme commitments, membership engagement, partnerships, fundraising, visibility and governance decisions. Institute quarterly implementation reviews and prepare concise performance briefs for the Board. Identify implementation bottlenecks, emerging risks and opportunities and recommend corrective measures. Coordinate periodic strategy reviews and contribute evidence for the development of ACE-AJ’s post-2030 strategic direction. 4.3 Holistic and People-Centred Justice Advance ACE-AJ’s agenda on holistic justice delivery by connecting formal, informal and community-based justice actors and approaches. Promote recognition of community-based justice practitioners and strengthen their contribution to accessible, affordable and responsive justice systems. Support member initiatives that demonstrate how legal empowerment, mediation, community justice, legal aid and other people-centred approaches can complement formal justice institutions. Facilitate cross-country learning on enabling policy and regulatory environments for community-based justice and paralegal practice. Ensure that the perspectives of poor, vulnerable and marginalised communities remain central to ACE-AJ’s programmes, research, advocacy and institutional narrative. 4.4 Capacity Building and Peer Learning Develop and coordinate a continental capacity-building programme informed by member needs and the Strategy. Organise practical peer-to-peer learning, mentorship, technical exchanges and cross-country exposure among members. Develop partnerships with universities, legal aid clinics, professional bodies, judiciaries and specialist institutions for training, research and professional development. Promote learning models that draw systematically on the experience of ACE-AJ members rather than relying exclusively on external expertise. Support development of scalable training resources and, where feasible, longer and more intensive learning programmes for community-based justice practitioners. 4.5 Research, Evidence and Knowledge Management Lead implementation of ACE-AJ’s research and knowledge-generation agenda, including practitioner-driven and comparative research with continental policy relevance. Coordinate documentation of best practices, innovations, impact case studies and lessons from member organisations. Develop and maintain an accessible knowledge-sharing platform or e-repository for research, laws, policies, tools, case studies and member resources. Promote common or compatible data-collection approaches across members to strengthen the African evidence base on access to justice. Coordinate research partnerships with universities, research institutions and practitioners and ensure appropriate ethical, data-protection and quality standards. Translate research into policy briefs, position papers, learning products, advocacy messages and practical tools for members and decision-makers. 4.6 Continental Advocacy, Policy Influence and Representation Develop and coordinate ACE-AJ’s continental advocacy agenda, drawing on member evidence and experience. Support development of coherent African positions on legal empowerment, community justice, legal aid, people-centred justice and related emerging issues. Build structured engagement with the African Union, African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, regional economic communities, United Nations mechanisms and other relevant regional and global institutions. Identify opportunities for ACE-AJ and its members to contribute to justice-sector reform, policy processes, legislative discussions and international forums. Represent ACE-AJ at authorised regional, continental and international engagements and prepare high-quality briefs, statements and speaking points. Ensure that ACE-AJ’s advocacy elevates member expertise and community experience rather than substituting for them. 4.7 Strategic Communication, Visibility and African Narrative Lead implementation of an institutional communication and visibility plan that establishes ACE-AJ as a recognised source of African expertise on access to justice and legal empowerment. Oversee regular member updates, newsletters, website content, social media, publications and other institutional communication. Develop a compelling evidence-based continental narrative demonstrating ACE-AJ’s added value and the contribution of its members. Increase dissemination and citation of ACE-AJ research, policy products and member-generated knowledge. Coordinate media engagement and ensure consistent branding, messaging and recognition of member organisations. 4.8 Resource Mobilisation and Financial Sustainability Develop, maintain and drive a diversified resource-mobilisation strategy and funding pipeline aligned with ACE-AJ’s strategic priorities. Map foundations, bilateral and multilateral partners, international organisations, corporate and philanthropic actors and other potential supporters. Lead or coordinate high-quality concept notes, proposals, budgets, partnership submissions and donor presentations. Build and maintain long-term donor and strategic-partner relationships and coordinate due diligence, negotiations, stewardship and reporting. Explore sustainable non-grant income approaches consistent with ACE-AJ’s mandate, governance and applicable legal requirements. Work with the host institution and relevant governance structures to ensure sound grant management, financial controls, compliance and transparent reporting. Strengthen ACE-AJ’s ability to demonstrate impact as a central element of fundraising and partnership development. 4.9 Programme Development, Multi-country Implementation and Accountability Design and coordinate multi-country and network-wide initiatives from concept development through implementation, monitoring, learning and reporting. Develop clear implementation arrangements with participating members, including roles, deliverables, budgets, timelines, reporting requirements and decision-making arrangements. Track delivery across countries and intervene early where implementation is delayed or quality is at risk. Coordinate narrative and management reporting to the Board, members, partners and donors. Ensure programmes demonstrate clear value to participating members and contribute to ACE-AJ’s strategic outcomes rather than operating as isolated projects. 4.10 Governance and Institutional Development Provide high-quality technical and administrative support to the Board and General Assembly. Coordinate AGMs, Board meetings and other governance processes, including agendas, briefing papers, minutes, decision registers and systematic follow-up. Maintain constitutional, governance, membership, programme and institutional records. Support development, review and implementation of policies, manuals, procedures and internal systems required for a credible continental institution. Ensure Secretariat operations comply with the ACE-AJ Constitution, approved policies, governance decisions and relevant legal and contractual obligations. Support the establishment and effective operation of thematic working groups, committees, patrons or other mechanisms provided for in ACE-AJ’s strategic and governance framework. 5. Expected Results and Performance Indicators ACE-AJ functions as an active, connected and member-owned continental network with demonstrably regular and substantive member participation. Annual strategic priorities and governance decisions are implemented, tracked and reported systematically. Membership expands strategically and becomes more geographically and linguistically representative. Regional and continental exchanges, working groups and joint initiatives produce documented learning and collaborative action. ACE-AJ generates and disseminates credible African evidence, research, best practices and policy products. ACE-AJ’s visibility and participation in relevant African and international justice platforms increases. A credible and diversified funding pipeline is maintained, with stronger donor stewardship and institutional sustainability. Multi-country programmes demonstrate timely delivery, accountability, learning and clear value to participating members. Governance, programme, financial, membership, partnership and communication records are accurate, current and accessible. ACE-AJ increasingly contributes an identifiable African voice to debates and policy processes on access to justice, legal empowerment and people-centred justice. 6. Qualifications and Experience Master’s degree in law, Human Rights, Development Studies, Public Policy, International Relations, Governance, Programme Management or a closely related field. A strong bachelor’s degree combined with substantial relevant senior experience may be considered. At least 5 years of progressively responsible professional experience in access to justice, legal empowerment, human rights, governance, civil society strengthening, international development, network leadership or a closely related field. Demonstrated experience coordinating a network, coalition, secretariat, regional platform or multi-country partnership. Substantial experience working across several African countries is strongly preferred. Demonstrated ability to translate strategy into implementation plans, budgets, partnerships, programmes and measurable results. Strong experience in programme design and management, monitoring and learning, budgeting, reporting and institutional planning. Proven experience in resource mobilisation, proposal development and donor or strategic-partner relationship management. Experience supporting governance bodies and organisational/institutional development. Experience in research, policy engagement, advocacy, knowledge management or capacity development relevant to access to justice is highly desirable. Excellent written and spoken English. Working knowledge of French is a strong advantage; knowledge of other widely used African languages is an asset. 7. Core Competencies and Leadership Profile Continental network leadership and movement building. Strategic execution and disciplined follow-through. Member engagement, coalition management and cross-cultural diplomacy. Resource mobilisation, partnership development and donor stewardship. Programme leadership and multi-country coordination. Governance, institutional development and accountability. Research literacy, evidence use and knowledge translation. High-level writing, communication, advocacy and representation. Sound judgement, political and institutional sensitivity, integrity and independence. Ability to work effectively across borders, time zones, institutions and professional cultures with limited supervision. 8. Particular Profile Sought ACE-AJ is seeking an Executive Coordinator who can build an institution and a continental network at the same time. The successful candidate will be comfortable engaging organisational leaders, practitioners, community-justice actors, academics, donors, governments, regional institutions and international partners. The person must be able to create trust among members while maintaining delivery discipline and accountability. Candidates should demonstrate through concrete examples how they have coordinated networks or multi-country partnerships; converted strategy into implementation; maintained active member participation; handled competing institutional interests; mobilised resources; built strategic partnerships; convened diverse actors; generated or used evidence for policy influence; and contributed to institutional growth, visibility and sustainability. 9. Reporting, Supervision and Working Relationships The Executive Coordinator shall report to the ACE-AJ Founding Members in accordance with the Constitution and shall operate within the agreed hosting arrangements with LAF. The Executive Coordinator will work closely with the Chairperson and other Board members, the General Assembly, member organisations and designated focal persons. For hosted administrative functions, the Executive Coordinator will maintain close operational coordination with the Executive Director and relevant departments of LAF. The Executive Coordinator will supervise ACE-AJ Secretariat personnel and coordinate consultants, technical advisers, interns, service providers and staff designated by member organisations to support ACE-AJ activities, subject to approved structures and budgets. 10. Eligibility and Right to Work in Rwanda This recruitment is primarily intended for Rwandan nationals and non-Rwandan nationals who are already legally resident in Rwanda and authorised to work in Rwanda. Due to the resources available for this position, ACE-AJ/LAF will not provide international relocation, expatriate benefits, or sponsorship for relocation to Rwanda. Applicants must therefore be able to take up the position in Kigali under an existing lawful right to reside and work in Rwanda. 11. Application Requirements Applicants should submit a curriculum vitae, a letter of motivation, copies of relevant degree(s) and certificate(s), and two professional references. The motivation letter should specifically demonstrate experience in coordinating networks, coalitions or multi-country partnerships and provide concrete examples of continental or cross-country coordination, strategy implementation, convening, membership engagement, partnership development and resource mobilisation. Applications should be addressed to the Executive Director of LAF, as host of the ACE-AJ Secretariat, and submitted by email to legalaidrwanda@gmail.com with a copy (cc) to ace.a2j@gmail.com The deadline for submission of applications is 30 October 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. Apply

The role owns process control, preventive and corrective maintenance, and quality and food safety compliance across the plant, while leading shift teams and operators. Set, monitor, and adjust process parameters (line speeds, temperatures, and processing times) to keep output consistent. Develop and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) for every line and piece of equipment. Identify bottlenecks and lead continuous improvement to raise throughput and reduce waste. Coordinate with harvest, logistics, and sales teams so that raw material intake matches plant capacity and orders. 2. Production Reporting & KPIs Track and report daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs, including throughput, downtime, yield, and waste. Analyze performance trends and present root causes and action plans to management. Maintain accurate production, maintenance, and quality records. Support budgeting for plant operations, maintenance, and spare parts. Strong process control skills and proven experience running preventive and corrective maintenance programs. Working knowledge of quality control and food safety standards such as HACCP, GMP, or ISO 22000. Cold chain or perishable-product experience is a strong plus. Proven ability to lead shift teams and operators in a production environment. Comfortable with production reporting and KPIs such as throughput, downtime, and yield; good working knowledge of Excel. Rwandan national, or already holding the right to work in Rwanda (Kivu Choice is not able to sponsor work permits for this role). Description Générale : Le responsable Risque et Conformité est le garant de la conception et la mise en place des stratégies permettant une meilleure surveillance et prévention contre toutes sortes de risques de la société ATLANTIQUE MICROFINANCE RWANDA. B. Missions principales : Elaborer le registre des risques ; Identifier et évaluer les différents types de risques (financiers, opérationnels, de crédit, de marché, de liquidité, etc.) auxquels l'institution pourrait être exposée. Développer la cartographie des risques de l’institution Mettre en place des mécanismes de surveillance pour assurer un suivi continu des risques et ajuster les stratégies en fonction de l’évolution de l’environnement économique et réglementaire. Élaborer et proposer des mesures de mitigation des risques afin de réduire les risques à un niveau acceptable. Suivre l’évolution des lois, régulations et normes applicables au secteur de la microfinance, tant au niveau national qu’international. Vérifier que l'ensemble des opérations et activités de la microfinance respecte les exigences légales, réglementaires et les bonnes pratiques du secteur. Préparer et soumettre les rapports requis par les autorités de régulation, en s'assurant de leur exactitude et de leur conformité. Former les collaborateurs sur les pratiques de gestion des risques et de conformité. Développer des politiques et des procédures internes adaptées à la gestion des risques et à la conformité pour l'ensemble du personnel. Identifier, traiter et résoudre rapidement les situations de non-conformité ou les incidents de risques qui pourraient affecter l’intégrité et la réputation de la microfinance. Développer des plans d'action de gestion des risques et conformités. Fournir des rapports réguliers à la direction générale sur l'état de la gestion des risques et de la conformité au sein de l’institution. Communiquer et entretenir des relations avec les autorités réglementaires, en veillant à la transparence et à la bonne conduite de la microfinance. Mettre en œuvre et maintenir le programme de lutte contre le blanchiment d'argent et le financement du terrorisme. La maîtrise de différents outils technologiques ; La maîtrise des normes de sécurité financière, organisationnelle, écologique... Bonne connaissance des principes et pratiques de gestion des risques financiers Intégrité, rigueur, esprit d’analyse et de synthèse. Bonne aptitude managériale. raw_text: Job Description: General Practitioner (GP) Department/Unit: Ketamine Treatment & Research Center (KTRC)Duty Station: King Faisal Hospital Rwanda, KigaliReports to: Designated KTRC Clinical Lead / Head of DepartmentEmployment Terms: 1 year renewable Position Overview The General Practitioner (GP) will provide medical assessment, monitoring, and follow-up care for patients receiving ketamine-assisted treatment at the Ketamine Treatment & Research Center (KTRC). Working closely with psychiatrists, nurses, psychologists, and other healthcare professionals, the GP will identify and manage medical risks, respond to adverse events, and ensure safe, coordinated patient care in accordance with approved clinical protocols, hospital policies, and applicable professional and regulatory standards. Key Responsibilities Conduct medical histories and physical examinations, review medications and comorbidities, identify contraindications and drug interactions, and request appropriate investigations or specialist assessments. Assess patients' medical status before treatment and communicate relevant findings and recommendations to the treating psychiatrist and multidisciplinary team. Monitor patients during treatment sessions in collaboration with the nursing team and respond to medical complications within professional competence. Recognize clinical deterioration, adverse reactions, and emergencies, initiate appropriate interventions, and activate hospital emergency pathways when necessary. Assess medical stability and discharge readiness, provide post-treatment precautions, and coordinate referrals and follow-up care. Participate in multidisciplinary case discussions and collaborate with the clinical team to ensure continuity and quality of care. Maintain accurate, timely, and confidential clinical records, including assessments, monitoring observations, interventions, and adverse events. Contribute to clinical audits, quality improvement, safety protocol reviews, and approved research activities in accordance with ethics approvals and confidentiality requirements. Comply with hospital policies, infection prevention standards, medication safety requirements, professional ethics, and continuing professional development requirements. Authority and Accountability The GP shall perform medical assessments, monitoring, interventions, and follow-up within the limits of professional registration, demonstrated competence, hospital privileges, and approved KTRC protocols. The GP's responsibilities include: Medical assessment and monitoring: Identifying medical risks, assessing patient stability, and supporting safe treatment delivery. Emergency management: Providing initial medical care, recognizing complications, and escalating cases requiring specialist intervention. Patient follow-up: Providing discharge advice, coordinating referrals, and supporting continuity of care. Documentation and quality improvement: Maintaining clinical records and contributing to audits, incident reporting, and approved research activities. Multidisciplinary collaboration: Communicating effectively with the treating psychiatrist and other healthcare professionals. Psychiatric diagnosis, psychiatric risk assessment, complex psychotropic medication decisions, and psychiatric treatment planning remain the responsibility of the treating psychiatrist. The GP shall not independently initiate or modify ketamine treatment outside approved protocols and the established authorization framework. Decisions regarding treatment eligibility, continuation, postponement, or discontinuation shall follow the designated clinical decision-making process. Qualifications and Experience Essential Bachelor's degree in Medicine or an equivalent recognized medical qualification. At least two (2) years of clinical experience as a medical practitioner. Valid registration and current practicing license from the relevant Rwandan medical regulatory authority. Demonstrated competence in medical assessment, clinical decision-making, and recognition of medical emergencies. Current Basic Life Support (BLS) certification, or willingness to obtain it within the timeframe specified by the hospital. Strong communication, clinical documentation, and teamwork skills. Commitment to patient safety, confidentiality, professional ethics, and adherence to clinical protocols. Preferred Additional training in general practice, family medicine, internal medicine, or emergency medicine. Advanced Life Support (ALS) or equivalent emergency-care training. Experience in outpatient, day-care, or procedural services involving patient monitoring. Experience in mental health, substance use disorders, or psychiatric comorbidities. Training or experience in ketamine treatment or ketamine-assisted psychotherapy. Experience in clinical research, clinical audit, quality improvement, or electronic medical records. Required Technical and Clinical Skills Medical assessment and clinical decision-making. Identification of medical risks, contraindications, and drug interactions. Patient monitoring and initial management of medical emergencies. Medication safety and clinical documentation. Emergency response, referral, and escalation procedures. Multidisciplinary teamwork and patient communication. Patient safety, confidentiality, and infection prevention. Basic computer literacy and electronic medical record management. TCP Africa implements the KoraLink Program (2025–2028), a joint initiative of the Mastercard Foundation and The Commons Project Foundation, in partnership with the Government of Rwanda, Society for Family Health (SFH) Rwanda, and the Rwanda ICT Chamber. KoraLink recruits, trains, and equips young people, particularly young women in rural and poor-urban areas, as “KoraLink Agents”: community-based digital sales agents who sell health and essential household products and services to their communities through a digital marketplace. Within TCP Africa, the Business Development function builds and manages the Program’s supply-side and employer partnerships, including manufacturers, distributors, vendors, and SMEs, so that KoraLink Agents have consistent access to a well-priced, well-performing mix of products, services, and other earning opportunities. Gushyiraho no gukurikirana agace kabuzanyijwe ku mpande z'aho imashini ihindukirira, inzira z'iminyururu, ahashobora gufatirwa, imitwe ikata n'ikusanya, convoyeur na tailpiece; guhagarara ako kanya igihe umuntu yinjiye mu gace kabuzanyijwe. Gukorera ku ruhande rwagenewe umutekano ahari ubutaka bushyigikiwe, ureba neza imashini, aho bacukura n'aho amabuye atwarirwa; ntuzahagarare iruhande rw'imashini igenda cyangwa munsi y'igisenge kidashyigikiwe. Kwemeza ko umwuka ukenewe, imyenda ihumeka (curtains), imiyoboro, scrubber n'ibitera amazi biri mu mwanya ukwiye kandi bikora neza; gukora ibipimo by'imyuka bisabwa, ugahagarara, ukazimya imashini ukavamo igihe guhumeka kwanze cyangwa imyuka igeze ku rwego rusaba gufata ingamba. Kudakata hatariho umuvuduko w'amazi ukwiye, ibitera amazi, scrubber n'ibikusanya ivumbi; kugenzura umwuka usubira inyuma no kubuza abantu kwegera ivumbi n'umwuka usubira inyuma. Gutanga impuruza, kugenzura inzira no kugenda buhoro; kurinda insinga, ibigenzura guhumeka, ibishyigikira ubutaka n'abantu, kwita ku hasi habi no guhuza umutwe ukata n'umurongo wo gukata wemewe. Guhuza gusuka n'imodoka zitwara (shuttle cars), amakamyo cyangwa ubundi bwikorezi ukoresheje ibimenyetso byemewe; kugumana intera, kubuza umuntu kwinjira hagati y'imashini no guhagarara igihe kugaragara, itumanaho cyangwa guhuza bibuze. Kutarenza intera ntarengwa yemewe idashyigikiwe cyangwa ubujyakuzimu bwo gukata; igihe ugeze ku mupaka, uhagarare, umanure ukingire umutwe, uhave, utegereze ko hashyirwaho ibishyigikira kandi ko guhumeka kwiyongera mbere yo gutangira. Kuzuza inyandiko zo gutangira, imyuka, guhumeka, umusaruro, guhindura ibyuma bikata, inenge, gusana, PTO n'ubushobozi, no gutanga raporo ako kanya y'impanuka, ibyenda kuba impanuka n'ibigenzura byananiwe. Kubahiriza Itegeko ry'Ubucukuzi N° 072/2024 ryo mu Rwanda, ibisabwa by'ubuzima n'umutekano mu kazi bireba ubucukuzi, ibisabwa na Rwanda Mines, Petroleum and Gas Board, amategeko y'ikirombe cya Trinity Musha, uburyo bwemewe bwo guhumeka, gufata ubutaka, gutwara no gutandukanya amashanyarazi, uburyo bwo gukoresha Continuous Miner n'igitabo cy'uwakoze imashini (OEM manual). 2. Ibisabwa ku Kazi, Ubushobozi n'Imyitwarire: Kuba ufite uruhushya rwo gutwara ibinyabiziga rwa category B na F Uburambe bw' imyaka nibura itatu(3) muri uyu mwuga. Icyitonderwa: Usaba ku mwanya wa LHD/ Scoop Tram Operator, agomba kuba azi gukoresha Wheel loader Usaba ku mwanya wa Continuous Miner, agomba kuba azi gukoresha Excavator Kurangiza neza amahugurwa y'ikigo (induction) n'amahugurwa yemewe y'inyigisho n'ay'ibikorwa ya Machine Operator. Isuzuma ry'ubushobozi mu bikorwa no kwemererwa ku mugaragaro gukoresha ubwoko n'icyitegererezo cy'imashini, sisitemu ya remote-control n'agace ahabwa gukoreramo. Icyemezo cy'ubuzima gifite agaciro gikwiriye gukoresha ibikoresho bigendanwa munsi y'ubutaka n'imbaraga z'umubiri uyu murimo usaba. Kugaragaza ubumenyi ku buryo bwo gukata, gahunda zo guhumeka no gufata ubutaka, kurwanya ivumbi, gupima imyuka, gutandukanya no gufunga amashanyarazi, umutekano wa remote-control, uduce tubuzanyijwe, aho imashini zihurira n'ubwikorezi n'uburyo bwo gutabara. Ubushobozi bwo kumenya ibikoresho bifite inenge, ubutaka budashyigikiwe, guhumeka kwanze, imyuka irenze igipimo, ihindagurika ridasanzwe, ubushyuhe bukabije, ibyago by'amashanyarazi n'imikoranire idatekanye y'abantu cyangwa ubwikorezi. Ubushobozi bwo kugumana umwanya utekanye wo gukoreramo, kwita ku kazi igihe kirekire, kugumana remote-control no gutumanaho neza mu gihe cyose cyo gukata. Kuza ku kazi neza, gukurikiza amabwiriza mu budahemuka no kwemera gukoresha ububasha bwo guhagarika akazi igihe cyose ikintu gikomeye cy'ingenzi cyabuze. Umukoresha Utanga Amahirwe Angana Trinity Musha Mines Ltd yubaha ubudasa no kwakira bose. Twakira amabaruwa y' abakandida bose bujuje ibisabwa batitaye ku gitsina, ubwoko, ubumuga cyangwa inkomoko. As we continue to grow, we are looking for a detail-oriented and proactive Procurement Officer to join our team and help us source mining equipment, materials, and services efficiently, transparently, and at the best value. Key Responsibilities Purchase Requests and Planning Receive purchase requests from the stores and departments, and confirm that each one is properly completed and approved before any action is taken. Check the item description, specification, quantity and budget availability on every request. Plan purchases using stock levels and supplier lead times, and place orders in good time—ideally two weeks before consumable stock runs out—so nothing runs short. Combine similar requests where possible to obtain better prices and reduce the number of orders. Sourcing and Quotations Follow the procurement method set out in the company's Procurement Manual for every purchase, and obtain the quotations or bids that the method requires. Identify and maintain a list of reliable, approved suppliers for all goods, materials, equipment and services needed by the company. Compare the quotations or bids received on price, quality, delivery time and payment terms, and prepare the comparison for approval as required by the Procurement Manual. Negotiate prices and terms with suppliers in the best interest of the company, within the limits of the Procurement Manual. Confirm that the selected supplier is registered and can issue a valid EBM invoice. Purchase Orders Prepare and issue a PO to the selected supplier only after the purchase has been approved. State on every PO the item description, quantity, unit, agreed price, delivery date and delivery place. Record every PO in the Excel PO register, showing PO number, supplier, items, amount, order date, expected delivery date and status. Follow up with suppliers to make sure goods are delivered on the agreed date, and inform the requesting department and the store of any delay. Delivery, Invoices and Payment Support Work with the Store Keepers and the Equipment Store Officer to make sure every delivery is physically counted and matched against the PO, the supplier delivery note and the EBM invoice, and that the price agrees before the invoice is passed for payment. Resolve shortages, damaged goods, wrong items and price differences with suppliers, and arrange returns, replacements or credit notes. Hand over the complete set of documents (PO, delivery note and EBM invoice) to the Equipment Store Officer for receiving in QBO, and to Finance for payment. Supplier Management Evaluate supplier performance regularly on quality, delivery time, price and service. Handle any claim about the quality of goods supplied directly with the supplier, supported by the Store Keeper's and the user department's records. Keep supplier contracts, agreements and contact details up to date and filed. Report poor or unreliable suppliers to the Procurement Section Leader, with a recommendation on whether to continue buying from them. Records and Reporting Keep all procurement documents (requests, quotations, comparisons, POs, delivery notes, EBM invoices) filed in order and available for audit. Prepare a weekly and monthly procurement report showing purchases made, pending orders, late deliveries and cost savings. Ethics and General Responsibilities Act with honesty and integrity, and avoid any conflict of interest in dealing with suppliers. Do not accept gifts, favours or payments from suppliers or potential suppliers. Follow company procurement policies and procedures, and the applicable laws and tax requirements. Perform any other related duties assigned by the Procurement Section Leader. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, Economics or a related field [2-3] years of relevant procurement experience, preferably in mining, construction, or another heavy industry Professional certification (e.g., CIPS) is an added advantage Solid knowledge of procurement procedures, contract management, and tendering processes Familiarity with mining equipment and supply chains is an added advantage Strong negotiation, analytical, and communication skills What We Offer Competitive salary commensurate with experience Health insurance Opportunities for professional development and career growth A safe, collaborative, and supportive work environment How to Apply Send your CV and a cover letter to info@gamico.rw with the subject line "Procurement Officer Application" by 28th October 2026. title: Investment Lead
raw_text: About Inzira Creative Partners Inzira Creative Partners is the sector infrastructure for Rwanda’s creative economy, coordinating the Creative Rwanda consortium and connecting creatives and creative enterprises to markets, catalytic finance and policy. The Creative Rwanda Program is delivered through a partnership with the Mastercard Foundation and is led and coordinated by Inzira Creative Partners, in collaboration with Gahaya Links and MASS Design Group. Within the program, Inzira leads ecosystem coordination and financial inclusion. Nibigira, from the Kinyarwanda for “it guides us”, is our catalytic fund for young creative entrepreneurs. It offers finance designed around how creative work actually earns. There is no land collateral, repayment follows income rather than the calendar, and every investment comes with business support built in.About the role Most Rwandan creatives have never been offered finance that fits how they earn. We are building a fund that does, and we’re looking for an Investment Lead to build and run it day to day. This is a builder’s role. The fund is in its first cohorts. You will shape how it works in practice, from finding creatives who have never been considered bankable to seeing capital come back so it can go out again.What you’ll drivePipeline and origination Build a pipeline of creative entrepreneurs across Rwanda, including outside Kigali. Make sure the application process is open to everyone the fund is for. That means bilingual Kinyarwanda and English, accessible formats, and support for applicants who can’t produce a written plan. Assessment and investment decisions Assess creatives on their practice, the demand for their work and their potential, not only on credit history or collateral. Prepare investment papers and bring sector insight on creative business models, seasonality and risk. Make sure every investment is documented, with a clear rationale, repayment plan and follow-up. Portfolio and repayment Monitor the portfolio so repayment follows what creatives actually earn. Spot repayment barriers early and act on them, so capital returns and can be invested again. Inclusion and support Make sure the fund reaches young women, rural creatives, refugees and persons with disabilities, and track it in disaggregated data at every stage. Make sure every investment comes with support, from financial literacy, pricing and business planning to mentorship and market connections. Partnerships and growth Lead conversations with banks, microfinance institutions and fintechs to build a pathway from Nibigira into mainstream credit. Pilot finance for emerging creative sub-sectors and turn what the fund learns into the case for its growth. Who you are At least five years in investment, credit or portfolio management, ideally in inclusive finance, impact investing or SME lending in Rwanda or a comparable market. Working knowledge of blended finance, including grants, returnable grants and revenue-based or shared-risk structures, and comfort working within shared governance. Experience reading irregular cash flows and assessing businesses that traditional lenders turn away. Able to turn portfolio data into pipeline and product decisions. A degree in finance, economics, business or a related field. A master’s or investment qualification is an advantage. Fluent in Kinyarwanda and English. Familiarity with Rwanda’s creative industries is welcome but not required. The ability to learn a new sector’s business models quickly, and to respect them, is. How you work You see a creative’s portfolio, contracts and audience as evidence, and you know the difference between a risky business and an excluded one. You’re as comfortable at a cooperative meeting in the provinces as in an investment committee, and credible in both. You’re disciplined about documentation, because a fund’s credibility depends on it. You hold inclusion as both commitment and design principle. Women, rural and refugee young creatives, and persons with disabilities within the creative sector, are part of Rwanda’s future. What we offer Opportunity to help lead a vibrant, purpose-driven organisation that fosters creativity and community engagement. A collaborative, dynamic environment committed to creative and cultural impact. The chance to shape the future of creative finance and the creative economy in Rwanda, Africa and beyond. Details Full-time, two-year fixed term with a six-month probation, renewable. Based in Kigali, with regular travel across Rwanda. Reports to the Executive Director. Target start date: 1 November 2026.How to apply Interested candidate should submit their application no later than 31st October 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application. Women, persons with disabilities and candidates from refugee backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Appointment is subject to background checks and Inzira’s safeguarding policies Apply

title: Regional Human Rights Specialist
raw_text: Regional Human Rights Specialist, Africa Rwanda Full-Time GLOBAL CONSERVATION Job Description Reports To: Director, Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) Location: Kigali, Rwanda (or another WCS Africa hub location) Country Program/Sector: APAMU /Africa Program Position Type: Full-time Scope/Capacity: Africa-wide Coordinates with: APAMU Team, Rights & Communities, Rights & Communities Regional and National Staff, Regional Leadership Teams, Country Directors, Landscape Leads, Protected Area Managers, Law Enforcement Advisors, Program Development Teams, and Technical Working Groups About Us The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is a private, nonprofit U.S. organization founded in 1895. Its mission is to preserve wildlife and wild places by understanding critical issues, developing science-based solutions, and taking conservation action that benefits nature and humanity. With more than a century of experience, long-term commitments in dozens of landscapes, a presence in more than 60 countries, and experience creating more than 150 protected areas worldwide, WCS has accumulated the biological knowledge, cultural understanding, and partnerships necessary to ensure that wildlife and wild places thrive alongside local communities. WCS recognizes that nature and people are intrinsically linked, and that biological and cultural diversity are interdependent, mutually reinforcing and often co-evolved. Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities frequently represent the most active defenders of nature, and we believe that respecting and protecting the rights of Indigenous Peoples and local communities reflects our global commitment to equity and justice and is our best pathway to achieving durable conservation. About the Africa Program WCS manages one of the largest conservation portfolios in Africa, supporting protected and conserved areas, community-led conservation, key biodiversity landscapes, species conservation initiatives, and wildlife law enforcement efforts across multiple countries. Globally, WCS also supports Indigenous and Traditional Territories, a growing opportunity to center guardians of nature and to secure their rights. The Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU) seeks to ensure that conservation outcomes are achieved in a manner that applies WCS policies, principles and commitments. The Global Rights and Communities (R&C) unit provides guidance and tools across WCS countries to promote community conservation, ensure social safeguards and promote respect for human rights and positive relationships with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and other rights holders. This position will play an important role in coordinating and contributing to a standardized approach to human rights protection in Africa, with the guidance of APAMU, Global R&C and close collaboration with regional and country teams. Job Purpose The Regional Human Rights Specialist will lead and support the standardization of human rights integration and rights-based approaches across WCS conservation programs throughout Africa. The position will provide strategic and technical guidance to country programs and field sites to support human rights integration in conservation law enforcement, conduct human rights impact analyses, assist in investigation or fact-finding around human rights issues as requested, develop recommendations for country programs or landscapes to address human rights issues and risks, and oversee the review of rights-respecting Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for field operations. This position reports to the Director of Africa Protected Areas Management Unit (APAMU), and will play a critical role in the APAMU team in fulfilling the needs of a human rights based approach. The position will maintain a dotted line of reporting to the Senior Human Rights Specialist in Rights & Communities Global, for final approval and review of substantive human rights products and in order to coordinate with broader WCS policy and approaches outside of Africa. The position will also coordinate closely with regional and country level human rights, law enforcement, safeguards and communities staff. This position will require significant travel to remote field locations and sites where WCS works, and working with diverse teams from different country programs. The candidate will be expected to undertake planning and coordination as necessary with global, regional and country or site-level counterparts. Major Responsibilities 1. Human Rights Strategy and Integration Work with Senior Human Rights Specialist to ensure the implementation of WCS's rights-based conservation approach across all Africa programs. Coordinate with Regional Social Safeguards leads to support country programs and landscapes to integrate human rights into conservation planning, project design, budgets, monitoring, and reporting. Provide technical guidance on international human rights standards applicable to conservation programming. Promote alignment between WCS sites, country and regional level management, APAMU, and Rights & Communities. Support the development and review of organizational guidance, tools, frameworks, and operational procedures related to human rights. 2. Human Rights Impact Analysis and Risk Management Conduct human rights impact assessments and analyses for new sites and other situations as needed. Identify actual and potential human rights risks associated with conservation interventions and recommend practical mitigation and management measures. Contribute to the development and maintenance of systems for tracking human rights risks, corrective actions, lessons learned, and emerging trends across Africa programs. 3. Human Rights and Conservation Law Enforcement Work closely with the APAMU Law Enforcement Strategist and Senior Human Rights Specialist to provide strategic guidance on the integration of human rights principles into conservation law enforcement operations. Support law enforcement teams, site managers, and country programs to ensure that internationally recognized human rights standards are observed, and protocols are adequate for monitoring, and training. Support the development, review, and implementation of rights-respecting law enforcement policies, protocols, and operational guidance. 4. Development of Rights-Respecting SOPs Review Africa-level Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) that embed human rights principles into field operations as needed together with regional safeguards leads, based on WCS institutional policies. 5. Training and capacity building Design and deliver human rights trainings with a focus on practical application of human rights protection and human rights-based approaches in the context of field implementation, community conservation and conservation law enforcement (or equivalent) 6. Other tasks as needed Review protocols and process relating to mainstreaming of gender equity, respect for the rights of Indigenous Peoples, local communities, and underrepresented groups in program design and management. Contribute technical content for donor reports and organizational reporting related to human rights commitments and achievements. Qualification Requirements Advanced degree in Law or other relevant field with a specialization in human rights; a first degree with relevant experience and certificates can be accepted in lieu of an advanced degree. Minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible professional experience in human rights advocacy, research, policy or monitoring and reporting. Proven experience working directly with Indigenous Peoples, local communities, civil society organizations, and/or government stakeholders in the context of Africa. Fluency in English and ability to work professionally in French. Desirable Qualifications Experience in conservation programs or issues relating to conservation. Experience with grassroots advocacy or human rights defenders. Fluency in Portuguese or African languages relevant to program areas. Core Competencies and Skills Technical Competencies Strong knowledge of international human rights standards and frameworks, and regional African frameworks Knowledge of both civil law and common law based systems for law enforcement. Understanding of human rights-based approaches to conservation and development including institutional due diligence practices. Demonstrated experience conducting human rights assessments and risk assessments and to develop appropriate methodologies. Understanding of gender integration, Indigenous Peoples rights. Experience developing policies, guidance documents, and operational procedures. Professional Skills Excellent analytical and critical thinking skills. Effective at organization, time-management, and self-directed field work. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Strong stakeholder engagement and interview skills. Ability to work effectively across cultures and multidisciplinary teams. Ability to influence and support change across diverse country programs. raw_text: Description Job Title: Civil & Structural Technician Department: Infrastructure Duty Station: UGHE, Butaro, Rwanda Reports To: Civil and Structure Engineering Manager Employment Type: Full-time 1. JOB PURPOSE The Civil & Structural Technician will provide practical technical and maintenance support for the University's civil infrastructure, buildings, and external facilities. The position will be responsible for routine inspection, preventive maintenance, minor civil repairs, building-fabric works, site measurements, workmanship checks, defect reporting, and support to approved facilities improvement projects. The successful candidate should be a hands-on, multi-skilled technician capable of working independently on routine tasks while also supporting contractors, artisans, engineers and facilities staff. The position requires good practical knowledge of civil works, basic structural elements, building maintenance, drainage, paving, and general building fabric repairs. The technician will be expected to identify defects and unsafe conditions, carry out authorized remedial works, maintain accurate work records, and promptly escalate major structural, safety or specialist issues to the responsible supervisor. 2. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES A. Civil Infrastructure Inspection and Maintenance Inspect assigned external civil infrastructure and building elements on a routine basis. Inspect and maintain paths, paving, steps, surface drains, gullies, and minor boundary works. Identify and report on settlement, cracking, blocked drainage, trip hazards, erosion and other defects. Identify potential concerns affecting retaining structures or other structural elements and escalate them appropriately. Carry out authorized minor repairs and maintenance works. Clear authorized drainage blockages and maintain serviceable access routes. Coordinate with gardening and other maintenance staff where vegetation affects drainage, access or civil infrastructure. Maintain accurate inspection and maintenance records. B. Building Fabric and Minor Civil Works Execute approved minor civil and building fabric maintenance works. Undertake practical repairs involving finishes, doors, roofs, drainage and other related building elements where safe and within assigned competence. Prepare work areas, tools, equipment, and materials before commencing assigned tasks. Take measurements and quantities required for maintenance and repair work. Carry out minor masonry, plastering, concrete, paving, drainage and related repair activities. Inspect completed works for workmanship and identify defects requiring correction. Complete assigned snagging and remedial work. Maintain clean, safe, and organized work areas. C. Facilities Improvement and Project Support Support approved civil components of facilities improvement projects. Assist with site measurements, setting out, access arrangements and preparation of materials. Provide practical site support to engineers, project managers, and contractors. Monitor assigned works and provide observations on workmanship, materials, and defects. Assist with snag identification and closure. Support civil interfaces associated with projects such as drainage, water infrastructure, tanks, STP works, grey-water systems, fire-protection infrastructure and other facilities improvements as assigned. Maintain records of site observations, measurements, completed works, and outstanding items. Work within approved drawings, specifications, scope, and instructions. D. Contractor and Workmanship Support Support the Facilities/Infrastructure team in monitoring contractor activities within assigned areas. Verify dimensions, quantities and completed works where assigned. Observe workmanship and report defects or deviations from approved requirements. Assist in preparing areas for contractor activities and coordinating access. Participate in inspections and snagging exercises. Provide evidence of completed works and support project close-out documentation. Escalate major technical, structural or specialist works to the responsible engineer/manager. E. Tools, Materials and Work Planning Prepare required tools, equipment, and materials for assigned work. Ensure appropriate tools are used safely and correctly. Report shortages, damaged equipment, or unsuitable materials. Assist with material measurements and usage records. Maintain tools and equipment in good working conditions. Keep work areas clean and properly protected during maintenance activities. F. Health, Safety, Quality and Environmental Compliance Comply with all applicable workplace health and safety requirements. Conduct pre-work checks and identify hazards before commencing activities. Use appropriate PPE and safe working methods. Follow safe procedures for working at height, manual handling, dust-producing activities, access works and use of tools/equipment. Protect building users, staff, visitors and property while carrying out maintenance work. Maintain good housekeeping at all work locations. Promptly report hazards, incidents, near misses and unsafe conditions. Stop and escalate work where conditions exceed the technician's competence or authorization. Maintain required quality and maintenance documentation. G. Documentation and Reporting Maintain complete work orders and maintenance records. Record inspections, defects, measurements, materials used and completed works. Provide photographic or other evidence of completed works where required. Record and follow up on outstanding defects and snags. Provide regular updates to the supervisor responsible. Ensure assigned work orders are properly closed out. Maintain accurate records of safety observations, incidents, and near misses. 3. KEY DELIVERABLES The Civil & Structural Technician will be expected to deliver: Safe and serviceable external civil infrastructure. Timely completion of assigned minor civil and building maintenance works. Accurate inspection and defect records. Properly completed and documented work orders. Effective identification and escalation of structural and major civil defects. Quality workmanship on authorized in-house repairs. Effective support to contractors and facilities improvement projects. Timely closure of assigned snags and defects. Proper material and tool utilization. Compliance with health, safety, and quality requirements. 4. QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE Minimum Qualifications Advanced Diploma in Civil Engineering, Civil Engineering Technology, Building Technology, Construction Technology or related technical field. A recognized technical/vocational qualification in civil construction or building works may also be considered supported by relevant practical experience. Experience • Minimum 2–3 years of relevant practical experience in civil works, building maintenance, construction or facilities maintenance. • Practical experience in the maintenance of buildings and external infrastructure is highly desirable. • Experience working with contractors and multidisciplinary maintenance teams is an advantage. • Experience in an institutional, commercial, healthcare, educational, or similar environment is desirable. 5. TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES The candidate should demonstrate practical competence in: General civil construction and maintenance. Concrete and minor reinforced concrete works. Masonry and plastering. Paving and external work. Surface drainage and gullies. Minor building repairs and building fabric maintenance. Basic understanding of structural elements and common structural defects. Basic site measurement and quantity take-off. Reading and interpreting basic construction drawings. Basic setting out and levels. Identification and reporting of construction defects. Basic use and care for construction tools and equipment. Workmanship inspection and snagging. Basic maintenance documentation and reporting. Occupational health and safety procedures. 6. HANDS-ON / MULTI-SKILLED REQUIREMENT The successful candidate should be willing and able to perform practical hands-on duties rather than functioning solely in an office or supervisory capacity. The technician should be capable of assisting with or performing, within their competence and authorization: Minor masonry repairs. Concrete repairs. Plastering and patching. Paving repairs. Drainage cleaning and minor repairs. Kerb and walkway repairs. Minor boundary wall repairs. Door and building fabric repairs. Minor roof-related maintenance support. Painting and surface preparation. Basic carpentry-related building maintenance. General facilities repair and maintenance activities. Preparation of work areas and materials. Site housekeeping and protection. Where a task requires specialist engineering design, structural assessment, major construction, electrical/mechanical expertise or other specialist competence, the technician must escalate the matter to the responsible professional or contractor. 7. BEHAVIOURAL AND PERSONAL COMPETENCIES The successful candidate should demonstrate: Strong practical and hands-on attitude. Reliability and punctuality. Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. Good attention to detail. Strong safety awareness. Good problem-solving ability. Ability to identify and report defects accurately. Good communication and interpersonal skills. Ability to follow instructions, drawings, and technical requirements. Good work discipline and housekeeping. Ability to prioritize maintenance tasks. Professional conduct when working around staff, students, patients, visitors, and contractors. Willingness to learn and undertake different facilities-related tasks within the technician's competence. 8. REPORTING AND WORKING RELATIONSHIPS The Civil & Structural Technician will report to the Civil and Structure Engineering Manager and will work closely with: Civil/Structural Engineers. Facilities and maintenance personnel. MEP technicians. Project managers. Contractors and artisans. Procurement and stores personnel. Security and other relevant institutional departments. 9. AUTHORITY AND LIMITS OF RESPONSIBILITY The technician is authorized to undertake approved routine maintenance and minor civil works within their demonstrated competence. The technician shall not independently approve, design or execute major structural works or specialist works outside their competence. Structural defects, major cracks, significant settlement, major drainage failures, structural instability, major alterations and other high-risk or specialist works shall be promptly reported and escalated to the responsible engineer/manager. Major works and specialist contractor activities remain subject to the University's approved project management, engineering and procurement processes. 10. PERFORMANCE INDICATORS Performance will be assessed against: Completion of assigned maintenance work orders within agreed timelines. Quality and durability of completed repairs. Accuracy and completeness of inspection and maintenance records. Timely identification and escalation of defects and safety risks. Effective closure of assigned snags. Compliance with approved drawings, instructions, and work methods. Compliance with health and safety requirements. Proper use of tools, materials, and equipment. Effective support for projects and contractors. Good housekeeping and protection of institutional facilities. How to Apply Applicants should provide: (1) curriculum vitae, (2) degree, (3) a cover letter describing your interest in UGHE and relevant experience. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page. University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Organizational Profile UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system. UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima—PIH’s sister organization—and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade. Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team. Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse, and Sexual Harassment At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work—including community members—as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy. UGHE will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of fraud, harassment, sexual harassment and any form of systemic abuse or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures. Apply

title: Zero Out Of School Children Project Director
raw_text: ROLE PURPOSE The Government of Rwanda, through the Ministry of Education (MINEDUC), has signed a framework agreement with Educate A Child (EAC) to achieve zero out-of-school children (OOSC) at primary level. MINEDUC selected Save the Children as implementing partner, working in consortium with Humanity & Inclusion (HI) and NUDOR. The goal is improved access to, and retention in, equitable primary education for all Rwandan children. The five-year project (2023–2028) aims to enrol and retain 177,119 children at primary level by: (1) strengthening identification, enrolment, attendance and retention of OOSC at school level; (2) empowering communities and families to support enrolment and retention; and (3) strengthening policies, data and feedback systems on OOSC. The Project Director holds overall accountability for technical leadership, strategic and operational management, consortium coordination and donor compliance of the ZOOSC Project. In line with the Save the Children Operating Model (consortium/Chief of Party-type awards), the post-holder is the lead representative of the consortium, the primary link with EAC, MINEDUC and partners, and ensures quality, timeliness and value for money of all results, reports and financial management. The Project Director works closely with the Country Office SMT, the DPO (budget holder) and Save the Children US (Member) to ensure the award is delivered in compliance with donor and SCI requirements.
