title: Expression of Interest (EoI) for Supply of Office Cleaning Materials
raw_text: Expression of Interest (EOI) SUPPLY OF OFFICE CLEANING MATERIALS. Reference Number: 7000025573 Publication date: 15.10.2026 Introduction The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH is a federally owned international cooperation enterprise for sustainable development with worldwide operations. The GIZ Office in Kigali covers GIZ’s portfolio in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ Rwanda/Burundi implements projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Union and other commissioning authorities in the following priority areas: Sustainable Economic Development; Good Governance; Climate, Energy and Sustainable Urban Development; Digitalization and Digital Economy; and regional projects in the Great Lakes Region. The GIZ Office in Kigali is responsible for financial, administrative, and human resource management functions covering the GIZ activities in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ intends to engage a reliable supplier to supply cleaning materials regularly, as and when the need arises. Scope of services The selected supplier is expected to perform the following scope of work. Supply of cleaning materials and supply procedure The supplier is responsible for the supply of cleaning materials (such as toilet paper, paper towels, detergents and soaps, disinfectants, glass cleaners, air fresheners, mops and mopping cloths, brooms, dustbins and other cleaning consumables and equipment) as per the demand received from GIZ project offices in Rwanda. Purchase orders may be combined or may be for even a single unit, as and when the requirement arises for any category of items, under our framework agreement. GIZ will issue a purchase order indicating the needed items and the respective quantities. The format of the purchase order will be agreed upon after the EoI procedure has been finalized. Once a purchase order is issued, the supplier is responsible for delivering the respective items within up to 5 working days after accepting the confirmed purchase order. The successful supplier shall deliver the items to any GIZ office location throughout Rwanda. However, GIZ's offices in Kigali will remain the major delivery points, as indicated in each order. Quantitative requirements The quantities of cleaning materials to be ordered under this framework agreement are indicative and non-binding. They have been estimated based on the average monthly consumption of cleaning materials by the GIZ Office in Kigali over the previous two (2) years (2024 and 2025), as summarized in the table below. These figures are provided for the supplier’s planning purposes only and do not constitute a guaranteed order volume. Actual quantities ordered during the agreement period will depend on GIZ’s actual needs and may be higher or lower than the estimates below. Item / material Unit Estimated average monthly quantity (2026–2027) Toilet paper Rolls 2500 Paper towel (Essuie tout) Rolls 2000 Air freshener – 300ml Cans 300 Cleaning powder – 5kg Tubs/bags 10 Liquid soap multipurpose – 5L Jerrycans 100 Liquid hand soap – 5L Jerrycans 50 Cotton floor cleaning cloth/torchon Pieces 50 Block WC Pieces 200 JIK / Blue– 750ml Bottles 100 JIK / White – 750ml Bottles 100 VIM – 500g Tubs 200 Soft broom with wooden handle Pieces 8 Office dustbin, plastic with lid, approx. 10 L Pieces 100 Glass cleaner, spray bottle 500ml (windows, mirrors, glass doors) Bottles 100 Dish cloth Pieces 100 Dish cleaning sponges Pieces 1000 Mop bucket with wringer, plastic, approx. 15 L Pieces 15 Dustpan and brush set, hand-held with handle Sets 15 Reusable cleaning gloves, medium/large Pairs 100 Agreement period The service provision shall commence as soon as possible, at the latest in November 2026. The framework agreement will be concluded for an initial two (2) years, with the option to extend the agreement for a further one (1) year. The agreement can be terminated by GIZ by giving three (3) months' notice at any time without providing any justification. However, any purchase commitment or payment placed or in the pipeline prior to the issuance of the termination notice shall be fulfilled by both parties. Payment procedure The supplier may submit invoices to GIZ after delivery of the requested materials. Payment will be made upon certification of item reception, within a period not later than 15 days. GIZ will not issue any advance payment at any time throughout the agreement period. Format of tender Interested suppliers must submit their tender in English, in PDF format, comprising the following two separate parts: Technical offer – comprising all the supporting documents listed under “Required documents” below (proof of experience/letters of reference, registration certificate, VAT certificate and tax clearance certificate). Financial offer – the completed “Form of Price Sheet and List of Cleaning Materials”, with unit prices indicated in Rwandan Francs (RWF), VAT exclusive, for each item/category. The tender, including the prices quoted, must remain valid for a minimum of ninety (90) days from the submission deadline. Required documents Participating suppliers must provide the following documents: 3 letters of reference as proof of 3 years of experience in Rwanda supplying different brands/categories of cleaning materials to major multinationals, corporates or international organisations. The supplier should prove the capacity to maintain and take care of operational activities for a longer duration. A valid registration certificate (issued by RDB). VAT certificate (issued by RRA). Latest tax clearance certificate (issued by RRA). Technical assessment criteria Tenders will be evaluated in two stages: Stage 1 – Eligibility check (pass/fail): GIZ will verify that all documents listed under “Required documents” have been submitted, and that they are complete and valid. Incomplete or non-compliant tenders will be disqualified and will not proceed to technical evaluation. Stage 2 – Technical evaluation: tenders that pass Stage 1 will be scored against the technical criteria below. A minimum overall technical score of 70 out of 100 points is required to qualify for financial evaluation. No. Technical criteria Weight (points) 1 Relevant experience: number of years beyond the minimum 3 years required, and the scale/diversity of clients (multinationals, corporates, international organizations) served in Rwanda. 30 2 Range and breadth of cleaning materials/brands offered, matching the categories required under this framework agreement. 20 3 Delivery capacity: logistics/fleet arrangements, ability to meet the 5-working-day delivery timeline, and geographic coverage across Rwanda. 25 4 Quality management practices/certifications (if any) and ability to ensure continuity of supply (stock levels, backup arrangements). 15 5 Financial and organizational capacity to sustain a multi-year framework agreement. 10 Total 100 Submission of offer: The Expression of Interest should contain the following: Technical Proposal: Registration Certificate issued by RDB VAT certificate issued by RRA Evidence of tax clearance issued by RRA Technical Proposal (attached template for technical proposal MUST be used) Completed Self declaration of eligibility Financial Proposal: Financial offer indicates the all-inclusive total contract price, supported by a breakdown of all costs as described in the specification of inputs. Your EoI has to be submitted in 2 separated emails to RW_Quotation@giz.de until 25/10/2026 1.The technical offer has to be submitted in PDF format and as attachment to the email with the subject: Technical offer 7000025573 2.The financial offer has to be submitted in PDF format andthe price must be in Rwandan Francs and VAT excluded (if applicable) and as attachment to the email with the subject: Financial offer 7000025573 (you must use attached price sheet) If the emails exceed the default email size of 30MB, offers can be exceptionally submitted through https://filetransfer.giz.de/ Offers submitted through any other sharing platform, as google documents or similar will not be considered. Offers submitted in hard copy will not be considered. GIZ reserves all rights. title: Request for Proposals for Recruiting a Consulting Firm to Undertake an Assessment and Develop Actionable Recommendations for Strengthening and Scaling Up the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS) in Rwanda
raw_text: ACCESS TO FINANCE RWANDA Request for Proposals For RECRUITING A CONSULTING FIRM TO UNDERTAKE AN ASSESSMENT AND DEVELOP ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR STRENGTHENING AND SCALING UP THE NATIONAL AGRICULTURE INSURANCE SCHEME (NAIS) IN RWANDA. Subject of Procurement: RECRUITING A CONSULTING FIRM TO UNDERTAKE AN ASSESSMENT AND DEVELOP ACTIONABLE RECOMMENDATIONS FOR STRENGTHENING AND SCALING UP THE NATIONAL AGRICULTURE INSURANCE SCHEME (NAIS) IN RWANDA. Procurement Reference Number: AFR/RFP-STRENGTHENING NAIS/OCT/2026. Date of Issue: OCTOBER 16, 2026 REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS PROCUREMENT REFERENCE NUMBER: AFR/RFP-STRENGTHENING NAIS/OCT/2026. 1. Background and Rationale The Government of Rwanda launched the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS) in 2019 as a flagship agricultural risk-financing instrument to protect farmers against insured crop and livestock losses, strengthen resilience, and facilitate access to agricultural finance. The Scheme is implemented through a public-private partnership bringing together Government institutions, insurers, reinsurers, financial institutions, farmer organizations, veterinarians, loss assessors, development partners, and other relevant stakeholders. NAIS has now transitioned from its establishment phase into a consolidation and scale-up phase, marked by expanded coverage across crop and livestock value chains, growing awareness and uptake of agricultural insurance, increased claims support to affected farmers, and strengthened collaboration among sector stakeholders. However, important challenges remain around insurance literacy and uptake, product relevance and affordability, claims experience, data quality and availability, digitalization, integration with agricultural finance, actuarial and reinsurance arrangements, subsidy sustainability, and effective monitoring and evaluation. Against this backdrop, MINECOFIN, MINAGRI, and AFR intend to undertake an independent assessment to evaluate progress made to date, identify key achievements, lessons learned, and persistent gaps, and generate practical, evidence-based recommendations to inform the strengthening and revamping of the next phase of the NAIS. The assessment will be aligned with NST2, PSTA5, Vision 2050, the Financial Sector Development Programme, the National Insurance Strategy, Rwanda’s Disaster Risk Financing priorities, and relevant international good practices, ensuring that the future design and implementation of NAIS is responsive to Rwanda’s evolving agricultural risk landscape and broader financial resilience objectives. 2. Objective of the assessment The overall objective of the assessment is to generate a robust evidence base and practical, prioritized, and actionable recommendations to guide Rwanda in strengthening and transitioning the National Agriculture Insurance Scheme (NAIS) into a modern, sustainable, inclusive, market-oriented, and climate-smart agricultural risk-financing instrument. The assessment will evaluate the Scheme’s performance, achievements, and contribution during the InsuResilience Solutions Fund (ISF) and Commercialization and De-Risking for Agricultural Transformation (CDAT) implementation period; assess its value for money, financial and fiscal sustainability, market-development effects, and broader economic additionality; and identify the operational, financial, institutional, regulatory, and policy reforms required for the next phase. It will inform measures to improve farmers’ protection against agricultural risks; crowd in private capital and capabilities; deepen the agricultural insurance market and generate positive spillovers for the wider insurance sector; expand access to credit and other financial services; stimulate productive investment, enterprise growth, and commercialization; strengthen climate resilience and inclusion; and contribute to food security, improved rural livelihoods, and sustainable agricultural transformation. 2.1 Specific Objectives The assessment will pursue the following specific objectives: Assess NAIS performance, resilience, and development outcomes: Evaluate progress against the Scheme’s strategic objectives; assess its contribution to farmers’ risk resilience, recovery, livelihoods, and broader agricultural development outcomes; identify achievements, lessons, implementation challenges, and persistent gaps; and assess the effectiveness of operational, institutional, policy and governance arrangements. Assess the relevance, effectiveness, quality and inclusiveness of products and delivery: Evaluate product suitability, affordability, coverage, basis risk and performance in addressing farmers’ evolving risks; assess awareness, uptake, renewal, retention and satisfaction; and review the efficiency, timeliness, transparency and accessibility of enrolment, underwriting, loss assessment, claims settlement and digital delivery, with results disaggregated where feasible by sex, age, farm size, geography, value chain and vulnerability. Assess value for money, financial sustainability, and fiscal affordability: Evaluate public expenditure on premium subsidies and scheme administration against economy, efficiency, effectiveness, equity, additionality, and sustainability; analyse subsidy incidence, leverage of farmer premiums and private capital, unit costs and benefits, fiscal risks, and alternative scale-up scenarios; and assess pricing, claims, reinsurance, and risk-sharing arrangements. Where monetization is feasible, estimate indicative benefit-cost or social-return measures; otherwise, apply a transparent value-for-money scorecard. Assess agricultural insurance and wider insurance-market development: Determine NAIS’s contribution to market depth, competition, product and distribution innovation, insurer and reinsurer participation, professional and data capabilities, geographic and value-chain reach, farmer retention, and unsubsidized uptake. Examine whether public support crowds in or crowds out commercial products and investment, the potential pathway toward reduced dependence on subsidies, and evidenced spillovers to the broader insurance market, including rural distribution, digital infrastructure, insurance awareness, consumer trust, and uptake of other suitable insurance products. Assess private-sector growth, access to finance and economic additionality: Examine whether NAIS facilitates entry, investment and continued participation by insurers, reinsurers, financial institutions, intermediaries, aggregators and technology providers; assess its contribution to farmers’ and agribusinesses’ access to credit and other financial services, productive investment, adoption of improved and climate-smart technologies, enterprise growth and value-chain development; and clearly distinguish observed associations and plausible contribution pathways from causal attribution. Benchmark NAIS and identify strategic reform and innovation opportunities: Benchmark NAIS against relevant regional and international good practices; identify transferable lessons and practical opportunities for institutional, regulatory, product, delivery, digital, financial, and climate-risk-management reform; and define priority actions aligned with NST2, PSTA5, Vision 2050, the Financial Sector Development Programme, the National Insurance Strategy and Rwanda’s disaster risk-financing priorities. Develop a practical reform and implementation framework for the next phase of NAIS: Translate findings into a prioritized and sequenced implementation roadmap with clear responsibilities, indicative timelines, resource requirements where feasible, implementation risks, and a results-based Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning framework covering operational, financial, market-development, economic, inclusion, resilience, and broader development outcomes. Interested bidders must confirm their intention to submit a bid by Wednesday October 21, 2026, at 17h00 HRS CAT Any requests for clarifications to the RFP may be submitted by Monday, October 26, 2026, 17h00 HRS CAT. Please note that a mandatory minimum requirement for this tender is a fleet of at least two (2) trucks. Scope of Work The tender covers three specific categories of transport: White oil fuel distribution LPG distribution (Bulk and Cylinders) Lubricant distribution Summary of HSE & Technical Requirements As part of the onboarding and pre-qualification process, bidders must demonstrate adequate Health, Safety, Environment, and Quality (HSE) systems. The detailed requirements will be formally presented but the core minimum requirements include: General Compliance & Management: Valid operating licenses, comprehensive HSE management systems, adequate insurance cover, and strict adherence to all national and transit-country hazardous goods regulations. Personnel & Fleet Standards: Competent, medically fit, and product-trained drivers subject to a zero-tolerance alcohol and drug policy, alongside strict fatigue and journey management. Vehicles must be roadworthy, legally compliant (axle limits, speed governors, ABS), and equipped with GPS, firefighting, and spill response gear. Category-Specific Vehicle Vetting: White Oils: Verified tanker integrity, calibrated compartments, leak/pressure tests, and spill/fire prevention equipment. LPG: Technical integrity and emergency shutdowns (for bulk); or secure decking, ventilation, and strict cylinder stacking limits (for cylinders). Lubricants: Proper product segregation, secure packaging, and contamination prevention controls. Operational Controls: Acceptance of mandatory "safe-to-load/offload" inspections, strict adherence to Rubis site and traffic rules, and the provision of periodic HSE and operational performance reports. Note: Tender-stage requirements are for pre-qualification only. Shortlisted transporters will undergo further rigorous HSE, technical, and product-specific vetting before final award and depot access. Invitation to Bid Tender Reference:RICA12/10/2026 Date of publication: 20 October 2026 The Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture (RICA) invites bids from eligible and qualified firms for the Provision of Event Management Services for the Second National Symposium, to be held on 12 and 13 November 2026 at RICA Campus, Gashora, Bugesera District. The services comprise the supply, installation, operation and dismantling of an event tent with decoration, air conditioning, flooring, furniture, LED screens, sound, lighting, microphones, branding and simultaneous interpretation, as specified in Section 5 of this bidding document. This tender is conducted through open competitive bidding and is publicly advertised on Jobs in Rwanda, in line with Sections 16(C) and 22.2 of the RICA Procurement Policies and Procedures. It is open to all firms that meet the eligibility and qualification requirements in Sections 3 and 4, including proven experience in successfully organizing or providing services for at least two (2) national- or international-level events. The successful vendor will be required to complete all setup activities at least twenty-four (24) hours before the event day, as set out in Section 6. Failure to meet this deadline will attract the penalties stated in Section 8. Bids must be submitted electronically only to tenders@rica.rw no later than Friday, 30 October 2026 at 12:00 Noon (Kigali time). Bids received after this deadline will not be considered. Firms wishing to take part are encouraged to register their interest by email to feedback@rica.rw, giving the firm name and a contact person, so that they receive any clarifications and amendments directly. Section 2. Bid Data Sheet and Key Dates The information below applies to this tender. Where it differs from any other part of this document, the Bid Data Sheet prevails. Item Particulars Procuring Entity Rwanda Institute for Conservation Agriculture (RICA) Tender reference RICA12/10/2026 Procurement method Open Competitive Bidding (Sections 8.1 and 16(C) of the RICA Procurement Policies and Procedures). Approval: End-user DVC, Tender Committee, DVC – Operations & Finance, Vice-Chancellor. Event Second National Symposium, Thursday 12 and Friday 13 November 2026 Venue RICA Campus, Gashora, Bugesera District Lots One (1) lot. Language of bid English Currency Rwandan Francs (RWF), inclusive of all applicable taxes including VAT Bid validity Ninety (90) calendar days from the submission deadline (Section 22.2 of the Procurement Policy) Bid security Not required Performance security Not required. Contract performance is secured through the payment terms and penalties in Section 8. Advance payment Up to 30% of the contract price, only against an Advance Payment Guarantee from a bank licensed in Rwanda (see Section 8) Subcontracting Permitted only for simultaneous interpretation and specialized audio-visual equipment, up to a total of 30% of the contract price, and only if declared in the bid. The bidder remains fully responsible. Submission method Electronic submission only to tenders@rica.rw. Hard-copy submissions will not be accepted. Evaluation basis Lowest-priced bid that is substantially responsive and meets all technical and qualification requirements (Section 25.2, non-consultancy services) Enquiries and complaints All clarifications, complaints on receipt of bids and requests for feedback: feedback@rica.rw Key dates Activity Date and time (Kigali time) Publication of tender notice and bidding document Tuesday, 20 October 2026 Optional venue visit (recommended) Thursday, 22 October 2026, 10:00 Deadline for written clarification requests Monday, 26 October 2026, 17:00 RICA responses published and sent to all registered bidders Wednesday, 28 October 2026, 17:00 Bid submission deadline Friday, 30 October 2026, 12:00 Noon Bid opening Wednesday, 4 November 2026, 10:00 Indicative notification of award Thursday, 5 November 2026 Indicative contract and purchase order signature Friday, 6 November 2026 Site access for setup begins Monday, 9 November 2026, 08:00 Setup fully completed and ready for inspection Wednesday, 11 November 2026, 08:00 (at least 12 hours before the event) Event days Thursday 12 and Friday 13 November 2026 Dismantling and site clearance completed Sunday, 15 November 2026, 18:00 Section 3. Instructions to Bidders 3.1 Eligibility To be eligible, a bidder must: be a firm legally registered in Rwanda with the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), with event management, event equipment rental or a closely related activity among its registered business activities; hold a valid tax clearance certificate from the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) and a valid clearance certificate from the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB); not be debarred or blacklisted. In line with Section 6(iv) of the Procurement Policy, RICA will check the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority (RPPA) and World Bank debarment lists before any award. A debarred bidder is ineligible; not be bankrupt or under insolvency proceedings, and not have been convicted of corruption-related offenses in Rwanda or elsewhere. 3.2 Conflict of interest A bidder must not have a conflict of interest. Bidders must disclose any family, financial or business relationship with a RICA staff member, Tender Committee member or anyone involved in this procurement, and must submit the signed declaration in Annex E. A bidder may submit only one bid. Any undisclosed conflict of interest will lead to disqualification. 3.3 Prohibited practices Corruption, bribery, fraud (including misrepresentation of experience or qualifications), collusion with other bidders, coercion and obstruction of audits or investigations are prohibited. Any such practice will result in immediate disqualification and may lead to cancellation of the award, referral to the RICA Anti-Corruption Committee and to the relevant authorities. 3.4 Clarifications Requests for clarification must be made in writing to feedback@rica.rw by the deadline in Section 2. RICA will send its responses, without identifying the source of the question, to all bidders who have registered their interest and will publish them on the RICA website at the same time. Responses and any amendments issued form part of this bidding document. Bidders are responsible for checking the RICA website for amendments before submitting. 3.5 Preparation of bids Quote for every item in Annex C, in RWF, inclusive of VAT and all other applicable taxes. Prices must cover all costs of delivering the services: equipment, transport, installation, testing, technicians and operators on site for both event days, consumables, insurance, dismantling and site clearance. No additional charges will be accepted. State any discount clearly in the Bid Submission Form (Annex A). Unconditional discounts only. Complete the Technical Compliance Sheet (Annex B), stating the brand, model, size or capacity offered for each item. State the total electrical load (kW) of all equipment offered, so that RICA can plan the power supply. 3.6 Submission Bids must be submitted electronically only, to tenders@rica.rw , before the deadline. The server time stamp of the receiving system is the official time of receipt. Use the subject line: Bid RICA12/10/2026 – [Bidder name]. Submit all documents as PDF files, signed and stamped where required. Total size should not exceed 20 MB. Bidders will receive an acknowledgment of receipt. Bids may be modified or withdrawn only before the deadline. Late bids will not be considered. 3.7 Bid opening Bids remain inaccessible until the opening session, which will take place at least one day after the submission deadline in the presence of at least three (3) members of the RICA Tender Committee, including the Tender Committee Secretary. All bids received will be recorded in the Bid Receipt Register. 3.8 Confidentiality Information relating to the examination and evaluation of bids is confidential until the award is notified. Any attempt by a bidder to influence the evaluation will lead to rejection of its bid. Section 4. Qualification and Experience Requirements Because this is a national-level event of approximately 1,000 participants with a fixed date, RICA requires bidders to show that they have delivered events of comparable standing. The requirements below are mandatory and are assessed on a pass/fail basis. A bidder that fails any of them will not be considered further. 4.1 Mandatory event experience The bidder must have successfully organized, or provided event management or event equipment services for, at least two (2) national- or international-level events completed within the last five (5) years (between 1 October 2021 and the submission deadline). For this tender, a national- or international-level event is an event that meets at least one of the following conditions: it was organized by or on behalf of a government ministry, national agency, public institution, international organization, embassy or development partner; or it was a national or international conference, symposium, summit, forum, exhibition or official ceremony, with participants drawn from across Rwanda or from more than one country. For each event claimed, the bidder must provide in Annex D: the event name, client, venue, dates and approximate number of participants; a description of the services the bidder provided (for example tent, sound, lighting, LED screens, interpretation); documentary evidence of successful completion: a reference letter or certificate of good completion from the client, or a copy of the contract or purchase order together with proof of delivery or payment; and the name, position, telephone number and email address of a client contact person. The experience must be that of the bidding firm itself. Experience of a subcontractor will not be counted toward this requirement. RICA may contact the client references to verify the information provided. Any false or misleading information will result in disqualification and may lead to blacklisting. 4.2 Key personnel The bidder must name and provide CVs for the following personnel, who must be present on site during setup and throughout both event days: Position Minimum requirement Event / Site Manager (1) At least three (3) years of experience managing event logistics, including at least one of the events listed in Annex D. Single point of contact for RICA. Audio-Visual Technical Lead (1) At least three (3) years of experience operating sound, LED screens and lighting systems for conferences or large events. Interpreters (as required) Professional conference interpreters with proven experience in simultaneous interpretation for the required language pair (English-Kinyarwanda). 4.3 Equipment availability For the event tent (Item 1) and the LED screens (Item 5), the bidder must provide proof of ownership or a signed lease or rental agreement with the owner, together with the owner's proof of ownership. RICA may inspect the proposed equipment before award. Section 5. Scope of Work and Technical Specifications The vendor shall supply, deliver, install, test, operate and dismantle the following for the Second National Symposium on 12 and 13 November 2026. The quantities and specifications below are minimum requirements. Equivalent or better items are acceptable if clearly described in Annex B. # Item Minimum specification Quantity 1 Event tent White tent, for two (2) days, with capacity for up to 500 people. Weatherproof, with side walls and secure anchoring. 1 lot 2 Tent and stage decoration Tent ceiling and stage ceiling fully covered with white draping materials. 1 lot 3 Flower pots Decorative flower pots / potted plants placed around the tent and stage. Bidder to state quantity offered. 1 lot 4 Air conditioning Air conditioning units sufficient to cool the full tent. Bidder to state number of units and unit price per unit, and total cooling capacity (BTU/kW). 1 lot 5 LED screens Two (2) LED screen sets, each 5m x 3m, installed on both sides of the tent, with processors, mounting structures and operators. 2 sets 6 Comfort monitors Two (2) stage comfort (confidence) monitors for speakers. 2 units 7 Sound system (main tent) Five (5) speakers, digital audio mixer, four (4) handheld wireless microphones, sound cards, production PC, all cables and accessories. 1 lot 8 Lighting Ambient lighting around the tent and spotlights mounted on trusses for the stage. 1 lot 9 Lectern and panel microphones Two (2) gooseneck microphones for lecterns and six (6) speaker microphones for panelists. 1 lot 10 Lectern branding Printing and installation of lectern branding. Artwork provided by RICA. 1 lot of 2 lecterns 11 Backdrop banner Stage backdrop banner, 48 sqm, printed and mounted on a frame. Artwork provided by RICA. 48 sqm 12 Carpeted platform Raised carpeted platform/flooring covering the entire tent floor. 600 sqm 13 Banquet chairs Banquet chairs with covers. 500 pcs 14 Executive chairs Executive chairs for the stage / VIP area. 10 pcs 15 Side tables Side tables for the stage / VIP area. 5 pcs 16 Cocktail tables Cocktail tables with tablecloths. 20 pcs 17 Simultaneous interpretation Simultaneous interpretation for a hundred (100) participants for two (2) days, English ↔ Kinyarwanda, including interpreters, booth, interpreter console, transmitters and 100 receivers with headsets. 1 lot 18 Exhibition Tent Tent for 200 pax and deco for two days 1 lot 19 Exhibition Tent Flooring Carpeted Flooring 1 lot 20 Cafeteria Tent Tent for 200 pax and draping for two days 1 lot 5.1 General service requirements All equipment must be in good working condition, clean and of professional event standard. The vendor is responsible for the safety and security of its equipment and staff, compliance with health and safety requirements (including secure anchoring of the tent and safe electrical installations), and insurance of its equipment and personnel. This means that the tent, decoration, flooring, furniture, air conditioning, LED screens, sound, lighting, microphones, branding and interpretation equipment must be fully installed, tested and ready for inspection no later than 08:00 on Wednesday, 11 November 2026. A bid that does not commit to this deadline will be rejected. 6.2 Milestones # Milestone Deadline 1 Kick-off meeting with RICA event team and submission of detailed setup plan and site layout Friday, 6 November 2026, on contract signature 2 Site access and start of tent erection Monday, 9 November 2026, 08:00 3 Tent, flooring, decoration and air conditioning installed Tuesday, 10 November 2026, 12:00 4 All setup completed, tested and ready for inspection Wednesday, 11 November 2026, 08:00 5 Joint inspection and full technical rehearsal (sound, screens, lighting, interpretation) Wednesday, 11 November 2026, by 12:00 6 Correction of any defects identified at inspection Wednesday, 11 November 2026, by 17:00 7 Event operation with on-site technical team Thursday 12 and Friday 13 November 2026 8 Dismantling and site clearance Start after close of event on 13 November; complete by Sunday, 15 November 2026, 18:00 6.3 Inspection and acceptance RICA's designated event coordinator and the vendor's Event/Site Manager will carry out a joint inspection at Milestone 5 and sign a setup acceptance record. Stage 3: Financial evaluation Only bids that pass Stages 1 and 2 will be compared on price. If fewer than three (3) responsive bids are received, the Tender Committee will proceed as provided in Section 8.1 of the Procurement Policy, which may include evaluating and recommending award on the bids received where this offers value for money. Section 8. raw_text: TENDER NOTICE TENDER TITLE: HIRING A CONSULTANCY FIRM TO DEVELOP A PMIS FOR DUHAMIC-ADRI TENDER PUBLICATION DATE October 20,2026 SUBMISSION DEADLINE October 26,2026, at 03:00PM SUBMISSION LOCATION DUHAMIC-ADRI Head Office, Kicukiro-Niboye (Only hard copy submissions are accepted) INQUIRY CONTACT EMAIL procurement@duhamic.org.rw 1. Brief description of DUHAMIC-ADRI DUHAMIC-ADRI is a local Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) based in Kigali, Rwanda, established and legally recognized under Ministerial Order No. 943/05 of 12 July 1985. The organization operates in compliance with the applicable laws and regulations of Rwanda, including Law No. 058/2024 of 20 June 2024, governing non-governmental organizations. Vision A rural world responsible for its self-socio-economic development. Mission Supporting integrated initiatives for the holistic development of rural population in their struggle for self-reliance. Objective The Objective of the Organization is sustainable economic self-development of rural populations through strengthened community structures, capacity building, and integrated support services. Strategic Pillars Livelihoods and economic capacity development Environment protection and conservation Mobilization for social change and family promotion DUHAMIC-ADRI organizational sustainability 2. Tender background DUHAMIC-ADRI’s mission is to promote integrated rural development and support rural communities in achieving socio-economic self-reliance. To strengthen its project management and monitoring capabilities, the organization intends to hire an experienced company to develop a centralized, user-friendly, secure, and adaptable Project Management Information System (PMIS). Which will provide a common digital platform for tracking progress against approved work plans, indicators and targets, monitoring budgets and expenditures, and generating timely management and donor reports. Further details about the tender are provided in the Terms of Reference annexed to this letter Thank you for expressing interest in working with DUHAMIC-ADRI Done at Kigali October 20, 2026 MUHIGIRWA Benjamin Executive Secretary Attachment attachment_file_524b0a2acd76c6e98f0d

title: A Call for Expressions of Interest for the Supply and Service Provision by Pre-Qualified Service Providers for the Year 2026
raw_text: A call for expressions of interest for the supply and service provision by pre-qualified service providers for the year 2026 The African Evangelistic Enterprise (AEE-Rwanda) is a Christian, local, non-Governmental organization dedicated to working with children, youths, families and their communities to address the root causes of poverty. Agriculture sector expertise, equipment, seed, consumables supply, training, agricultural & nutritional consultancy and services Sport wear Hybrid car services/garage Air conditioning(ac) supply, installation and maintenance Supply of chickens Supply of pigs, piglets, goats, sheep Digital services provision (Apps, training) Kitchenware Import duty/tax clearing agents Supply of mats, umbrellas Provision of vehicle fabric roof covers/convertible roof coverings, rear guards and other related car protection services. title: Tender Notice for Provision of Hotel Services
raw_text: TENDER NOTICE PROVISION OF HOTEL SERVICES Pro-Femmes Twese Hamwe (PFTH) is an Umbrella of Rwandan Civil Society Organizations aiming at advancement of women status, peace and development. It was established in October 1992 and currently represents 52 member organizations within the country. The mission of Pro-Femmes/ Twese Hamwe is to eradicate all forms of discrimination against women, to promote their socio-economic political and legal status, and to enhance the institutional and organizational capacities of its member organizations through the promotion of sustainable human development approach based on gender equality and a culture of peace, justice and human rights. PFTH is thus looking for competent service providers to provide hotel services in the following locations: Lot 1: City of Kigali (Centre d’acceuils) ONLY; Lot 2: Southern Province (Nyamagabe, Nyaruguru, Kamonyi, Ruhango and Gisagara Districts); Lot 3: Western Province (Rusizi, Karongi, Rutsiro, Nyabihu and Nyamasheke districts); Lot 4: Eastern Province (Rwamagana, Kayonza, Nyagatare, Gatsibo, Ngoma, Kirehe and Bugesera districts); Lot 5: Northern Province (Rulindo, Burera, Gakenke, Musanze and Gicumbi districts). Tender Documents are obtained on any working day from 8:30 am to 5:00pm local time at PRO-FEMMES TWESE HAMWE Central Secretariat Office, upon presentation of proof payment of a non-refundable fee of ten thousand Rwandan francs(10,000Frw) to the account No: 1002190104949201 of PRO-FEMMES TWESE HAMWE opened in ACCESS Bank. Well-printed and properly bound proposals should be submitted (The technical proposal and financial proposal) in one Big envelope (outer envelope). The application shall be addressed to the Executive Director of Pro-Femmes Twese Hamwe and shall be submitted at PFTH central secertatiat, Head Office in Gahanga sector, Kicukiro district –Kigali City, not later than Monday 26th October 2026at 10:00 AM (Local time). Done at Kigali on 14th October 2026 Annet KAKIBIBI Executive Director

title: Request for Proposal for Supply, Installation, Testing and Commissioning of 30 kV / 0.4 kV Power Supply Infrastructure and a 315 kVA Distribution Transformer
raw_text: easyHATCH Ltd ("the Company" or "the Client") operates a poultry farm in Cyuve Sector, Musanze District, Rwanda. The farm's continued development requires a dedicated medium-voltage (MV) grid connection and an on-site distribution transformer. Following the Energy Utility Corporation Limited (EUCL)’s issued Supervision Quotation for the Power Supply to easyHATCH Ltd, setting out the technical design for the connection and a Bill of Quantities (BoQ) for the materials required. EUCL's quotation is for design supervision and final testing/commissioning oversight only. ! Purpose of this RFP easyHATCH Ltd is seeking competitive proposals from qualified, RURA-approved electrical contractors to supply all materials, and to install, test and commission the complete MV/LV power supply infrastructure described in Section 2 below — including the supply, installation and commissioning of the 315 kVA transformer — in accordance with EUCL's approved technical design and Rwanda's electricity-sector technical standards, and to EUCL's satisfaction at final witness testing. Kindly download the attached document for full details. Attachment attachment_file_64e606d036bc1f4ed566

raw_text: COOPERATIVE DUHAHIRANE GISOZI AMNDEMENT: INVITATION TO TENDER: 02/CO/DU/GIS/2026 TITLE: SUPPLY AND INSTALLATION OF PRINTER AND SERVER Cooperative Duharirane Gisozi invites qualified bidders to participate in the tender for the Supply and Installation of Printer and Server. The tender shall be conducted in one (1) lot. Participation is open, under equal conditions, to all specialized enterprises legally operating in the relevant field. Interested bidders may obtain the tender documents from the Cooperative Duharirane Gisozi office starting from 28 September 2026, upon presentation of a deposit slip for a non-refundable fee of RWF 10,000, deposited into Account No. 4076200015973 held at Equity Bank, in the name of Cooperative Duharirane Gisozi. Bids shall be prepared in English or French, properly printed, signed, stamped, and bound. Each bid shall be submitted in three (3) copies: one (1) original and two (2) copies. Bids shall be submitted to the Cooperative Duharirane Gisozi office no later than Friday, 23 October 2026, at 10:00 hours. All bids must be accompanied by a Committee Letter. The outer envelope shall clearly indicate the name and title of the tender. Bids shall remain valid for a period of ninety (90) days from the deadline for submission of bids. The site visit is scheduled to take place from 5 to 14 October 2026. Any amendments or changes relating to the site visit shall apply only to bidders who have not yet completed the site visit. Bidders who have already completed the site visit shall not be affected by these amendments.) All payments shall be made in Rwandan Francs (RWF). The opening of bids shall take place on the same day, Friday, 23 October 2026, at 10:30 hours prompt, at the Cooperative Duharirane Gisozi office, in the presence of bidders or their authorized representatives. title: Request for Quotation (RFQ) _Supply and Delivery of Pigs for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project
raw_text: Project/Activity Name Heifer International Rwanda Agresso Work order: RW1338 Country: Rwanda Advertisement for Procurement Request for Quotation (RFQ) Supply and Delivery of Pigs for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project. Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a Nonprofit and International Non-governmental Organization with the mission to alleviate hunger and poverty, while caring for the environment through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become theflagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. Heifer International Rwanda partners with smallholder farmers to build sustainable livelihoods by empowering them to use their own energy, ingenuity, and dreams to fuel their success out of hunger and poverty. Heifer programs mobilize communities and foster the organization of associations, cooperatives and social networks while strengthening their capacity to address development challenges. Purpose and Objective The objective of this procurement is to obtain the required quantities of livestock, meeting the prescribed technical and quality standards, and to deliver them to the designated locations in Rwanda’s Northern, Southern, and Western Provinces. How to Apply Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below. All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Pigs for PRISM Project” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 29th October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. Done on October 5th, 2026. Heifer International Rwanda Management Attachment attachment_file_efdda77c8e5b70e62ea3

title: Tender for Six Senior Software Engineering Trainers for Code Reviews (International Expert Positions) as Trainers for the Rwandan Software Development Trainee Program "1000 Intermediate Developers"
raw_text: Tender for six Senior Software Engineering Trainers for Code Reviews (International Expert Positions) as Trainers for the Rwandan Software Development Trainee Program "1000 Intermediate Developers" 1. General information 1.1 About KB21 KB21 Ltd. is committed to promoting the Rwandan IT scene. We focus on capacity developmentand job creation in the Rwandan IT economy. KB21 Ltd. has been partnering with Rwandan companies, institutions, and individual trainers in several projects, connecting Rwandan tech teams to international projects and remote work opportunities. In 2019, we introduced our independent training program, called “The Gym”, together with our partner Tech in Ruanda e.V., guiding young Rwandan ICT talent through a structured set of technology and professional skills modules empowering them to provide services for global clients. Later this program evolved into the “1000 Intermediate developers” program. 1.2 About “The Gym” and “1000 intermediate developers” The Gym is Rwanda's most intense software development trainee program. Trainees join the program with solid foundations in software development and undergo a rigorous 6-month, full-time, on-site training in software development, professional skills and ways of work that brings them to the level of being able to join international software development teams as Junior Developers. The 1000 intermediate developers program adapts The Gym’s 6-month full-time training into a 12-month part-time program that runs in parallel to university, targeting students at the beginning of their studies. After completion of the 12-month core training, successful graduates transition into the project phase of their traineeship, which lasts until graduation from university. The project-phase allows participants to grow to the level of intermediate software developers. Graduates of The Gym work remotely from Rwanda for international companies. Find out more on https://www.thegym-rwanda.com/ For this assignment: We are looking for six Trainers who have deep experience in working as a software developer in a European context, preferably a German context, as this is where most employers of the “1000 intermediate developers” program graduates are based. The Experts need to have immersed themselves in the ways of work in Europe on-site and need to have this experience from several companies, allowing for more representative impression and not the limited perspective of a single company. At the same time the person should have an initial understanding of the Rwandan context. They should have experienced working on-site in Rwanda, even if it is for brief period, so that the basics of working in the country are not completely alien. They should also have collected some experience working with Rwandan software developers from various companies. 2. Contractual information The service can be performed remotely. The service performance period is November 2026 to January 2027. The legal entity that is carrier of The Gym and 1000 intermediate developers is KB21 Ltd., a Rwandan limited liability company. Quotes for this tender can be specified in EUR or in RWF. Companies need to specify the individual trainers who will be conducting these trainings and share the information (CV, references etc.) related to that specific trainer. Companies will only be able to change the expert trainers during the duration of the contract with prior written consent of KB21 Ltd. When the trainers change, KB21 Ltd. will have the right to terminate the contract, if it does not consent to the change of trainers. 3. Tasks to be performed by the contractor Our trainees work on exercise projects in groups of approximately 4 people. Their work is peer reviewed and reviewed by coaches. But additionally, we want it to be reviewed by an international Senior Developer. This aims at ensuring highest standards of code quality and best practice adherence, but it also aims at exposing our trainees to the expectations and habits regarding communication style and ways of work that an international senior developer has. To this end we are looking for six international senior developers who will provide: approximately 2 to 2.5 hours of code reviews and technical help on complex exercise projects per group of approximately 4 trainees every week, depending on the coaching needs of the group. There will be 57 groups of trainees requiring this coaching, meaning that we are expecting approximately 135 hours of coaching per week across all groups. The coaching will be delivered by six coaches, with each coach responsible for approximately 9 to 10 groups. This will be done for a defined portion of the cohort period, totalling approximately 11 weeks (3 months). The total number of consultant hours is going to be 1,482 hours. Detailed task breakdown: Code reviews: Trainees use GitHub as a version control system and remote repository. When they work on exercise projects they share their code with the trainers through a pull request. Pull requests are either feature-based or they represent the coding progress done up to a certain point in time (e.g. via a dev->main PR at a certain predefined cutoff-date) The trainers then add detailed comments to individual lines of code in the pull request through GitHub's built-in commenting functionality. Comments relate not only to errors but also to best practices and code quality criteria. Comments need to be detailed and make the recommended improvement explicit. Trainees then edit their code and ask for a re-review. This continues until comments have been addressed to the full satisfaction of the trainers in which case the trainers mark the comments as resolved. When all comments have been resolved the trainers merge the pull request. Notifications about pull requests, comments, requests to re-review etc. are triggered through GitHub's built in notification functionalities. Additionally, they can be shared on discord or any other similar communication platform that is used for coordination between the trainers and the trainees. Technical help: The trainers conduct a weekly call with the trainees to talk through noteworthy issues identified during code reviews and to help with particularly challenging questions faced by the trainees. Trainees prepare questions for these calls about issues they are stuck on and share those questions with the trainers before the call. During the call the trainers provide ideas for how to solve the issue verbally and shares any resource-links in the chat of the call. In some cases, requests for such technical help may also be shared in between calls on discord or any similar communication platform that is used for coordination between the trainers and the trainees. 4. Tender requirements 4.1 Qualifications of the experts needed General professional experience: At least 5 years of experience working as a Senior software developer in a European context, out of which: At least 1-year experience in Germany; Within at least 3 different teams on-side in Europe. Specific professional experience: At least 3 years as a Tech Lead in Europe on-site, out of which: At least 1-year experience in Germany; Within at least 2 different teams on-site in Europe. Leadership / management experience: Lead developer teams in at least 2 projects with an international team-composition, including the participation of Rwandan developers in at least 1 project. Experience in the region / knowledge of the country: at least 1 project in Rwanda, e.g. short-term assignment working on-site, leading or training Rwandan software developers. 4.2 Specifications of input Tasks Number of hours/ weeks Total number of hours for the assignment Code reviews and technical help on complex exercise projects Technical coaching Approx. 135 hours per week 1,482 hours For the purpose of the financial bid, bidders shall calculate their price based on exactly 1,482 hours. This is the maximum estimated volume of services; KB21 Ltd. is not obliged to use the full number of hours, and payment will be made only for hours actually performed. The weekly volume of approximately 135 hours is indicative and may vary according to the needs of the assignment, within the overall maximum. 5. Requirement on the format of the tender The quote should include: A financial quote Evidence of commercial register entry A signed declaration by the company submitting the quote, confirming that none of the exclusion grounds listed in the “Eligibility criteria” section apply. Trainer CV The criteria table (can be merged with Trainer CV, for details see criteria table section below). Please make sure to provide a reference for each experience you mention in the criteria table. The structure of the tender must correspond to the structure of the ToR. In particular, the criteria table should be organised in accordance with the positively weighted criteria in the assessment grid (not with zero). The tender must be drawn up in English language. Criteria table Please submit a table in the format below. Use one row for each criterion, and list the name of the company / organization. The criteria table can be combined with the CV’s, as long as the matching between criteria and experience is made obvious. Criteria Experience Reference for each experience General professional experience Specific professional experience Leadership / management experience Experience in the region / knowledge of the country 6. Evaluation Criteria The technical assessment is based on this technical assessment grid. An offer will be selected, if the vendor is eligible and the offer ranks the best based on the combined reached points in the technical assessment (weighted 70%) and the price assessment (weighted 30%). 7. Eligibility criteria Eligibility criteria for this tender are: Evidence of commercial register entry Exclusion grounds: The tenderer must provide a signed declaration confirming that none of the following situations apply: Criminal convictions for corruption, fraud, money laundering, or other offences affecting professional integrity; Insolvency, bankruptcy, liquidation, or similar proceedings; Serious professional misconduct affecting the ability to perform the contract; Actual or potential conflict of interest with the contracting entity or the project. 8. Submission of Quotes, relevant dates Deadline for submission of quotes is the 05th of November 2026. Please submit your quotes by uploading them to https://www.the-gym.rw/Senior-Software-Engineering-Trainer-International-Expert Service provision is expected to start on the 09th of November 2026.

title: Tender Notice For supply and Delivery of Infant Formula at Rwinkwavu IMB Pharmacy Warehouse Under a Framework Agreement
raw_text: PUBLIC TENDER NOTICE # PIH/IMB/10941 /M10/FY27 TENDER TITTLE: SUPPLY AND DELIVERY OF INFANT FORMULA AT RWINKWAVU IMB PHARMACY WAREHOUSE UNDER A FRAMEWORK AGREEMENT. SOURCING METHOD: OPEN COMPETITION FOR DOMESTIC COMPANIES. Partners In Health (PIH) is a nonprofit organization with its headquarters in Boston, Massachusetts, whose mission is to provide quality health care for poor and most in need populations around the world. Since 2005, the Ministry of Health in Rwanda has worked with PIH Rwanda, also known as Inshuti Mu Buzima, to improve the quality of care in the country and increase health care access for Rwanda most in need populations. PIH/IMB have since helped to bring high-quality health care to three Districts namely: Kayonza, Burera and Kirehe. Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima is seeking proposals from qualified and authorized medical companies to supply infant formula at Rwinkwavu IMB Pharmacy warehouse under a framework agreement as per term of reference (ToRs) found in annex. Interested and qualified bidders should provide their proposals bearing the following requirements: BIDDERS/ VENDORS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA The bidders falling in any of the following categories will be ineligible to participate in this tender and / or its award: The Bidder should not be suspended or blacklisted by PIH-IMB or OnePIH nor blacklisted or revoked licenses by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or other relevant regulatory bodies. The Bidder should not have any ongoing contracts with PIH-IMB that demonstrates poor performance. Vendors or Companies owner must not be employed by PIH or One PIH within five past years, unless PIH seeks their expertise for consultancy services based on proven specialized knowledge. Any bidder that owns operates, or exercises controlling shareholding in more than one company is strictly prohibited from submitting more than one bid under this tender. Submission of multiple bids by related or affiliated entities under the same beneficial ownership shall constitute a breach of tender participation rules. NB: Non-compliance with any of above provision shall result in the annulment of bid examination process/ tender competition. COMPULSORY REQUIREMENTS: The Bidder shall submit a comprehensive Company Profile, including, but not limited to, the following: Company Identification; Physical Address and Contact Details; Legal and Registration Information; Nature of Business; Ownership and Management Structure; Relevant Experience and Capacity; Business Facilities including warehouse(s) and/or store(s); and Business Partners. III. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENT: The Bidder shall submit registration of domestic company issued by RDB in the same domain required. The Bidder shall submit valid RRA tax clearance. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Bidders should consider ToRs available in Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System following this link: (https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/index.php) FINANCIALLY, THE BID SHALL INDICATE: A commitment letter for the submission of the Performance Security (Bank Guarantee). title: Expression of Interest (EoI) for Supply Reusable Sanitary Pads
raw_text: Expression of Interest (EOI): Supply reusable Sanitary Pads Reference Number: 7000025524 Publication date: 15.10.2026 Introduction The Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH is a federally owned international cooperation enterprise for sustainable development with worldwide operations. The GIZ Office in Kigali covers GIZ’s portfolio in Rwanda and Burundi. GIZ Rwanda/Burundi implements projects on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development, the European Union and other commissioning authorities in the following priority areas: Sustainable Economic Development; Good Governance; Climate, Energy and Sustainable Urban Development; Digitalization and Digital Economy; and regional projects in the Great Lakes Region. Context GIZ Rwanda’s projects “Prevention of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence” and “ZFD – Supporting Peaceful Coexistence between Host Communities and Refugees” are part of the Rwandan - German development cooperation implemented by GIZ. Both work closely with civil society organizations. Their shared objectives are to strengthen and expand sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) prevention services and services around Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) provided by non-governmental actors and improving support for people affected by SGBV - both within and outside refugee camps. The projects intend to further strengthen the integrated approach on GBV prevention, SRHR and Menstrual Health and Hygiene and Period Poverty alongside peace peacebuilding and gender-based violence prevention It is in that context that GIZ is looking for a reputed and experienced company to supply the following reusable sanitary pads/items: The specifications and quantities are in the table below: Specification of items NO ITEM ITEM SPECIFICATIOM QUANTITY 1 REUSABLE SANITARY PADS Each pack should contain: 5 reusable sanitary pads. Reusable cloth pads with wings Medium size: 30cm length and 18cm width with wings Shall be able to handle normal and more heavily flow. A hanger for drying. Each pack should have one leak proof travel pouch to store a minimum of two soiled pads and shall be reusable. An info sheet;( must be multilingual English, French and Kinyarwanda) Instructions for use and shall include use, wash, and care instructions, preferably with illustrations or pictograms. Top sheet is made of fleece. The absorbent core is made of Microfiber. The reusable sanitary pads shall have securement mechanisms such as plastic snaps for the wings to firmly attach the product to underwear to prevent dislocation while use. Product shall be unscented only. The reusable sanitary pads are packed in an appealing, durable bag that can be closed with a zipper (it is not visible what is inside)" The pads shall be free from: acids and alkali, dust and particulate matter, bad odour bleeding of colour, shedding fibres chemical residues like chlorine, herbicides, pesticides, heavy metals. Products shall be capable of being soaked and washed thoroughly in water up to 60℃ using soap or laundry detergent. Wear Time: Shall be able to wear for 6 to 8 hours. Durability: the product shall be able to withstand a minimum of 120 washes during hand wash The seam line shall be free of loose threads and neat. It shall have dimensional stability with good tensile strength and seam strength. 2500 packs of 5 reusable sanitary pads each(therefore, a total of 12.500 reusable sanitary pads) Procedure The assessment is divided into three stages: Eligibility check, technical and financial evaluation: Eligibility criteria Participating companies must meet the following eligibility criteria: The company must have a minimum experience of 3 years in Rwanda supplying similar items to different institutions. three Letters of Reference from the past three years from such institutions must be provided. The company must possess a valid registration certificate (issued by RDB), VAT certificate (issued by RRA) and latest Tax clearance certificate (issued by RRA). The company must confirm in writing that the offer is valid until at least 4 weeks after the submission period has ended. Please submit the documentary evidence for the above criteria. Non-submission/Partial submission of commercial/technical documents mentioned above by any supplier will lead to a rejection of the entire bid. Technical Assessment The bidders are encouraged to include a company profile that displays they fulfil the eligibility requirements. The technical specification of each item proposed must meet the technical requirements as described above. The offer must provide clear and complete specifications of items proposed. As part of the technical evaluation process, GIZ will request eligible bidders to provide a sample of products based on the technical specification. This sample must be delivered to GIZ Rwanda’s Country Office in Kiyovu, 17 KN 41 St, Kigali within 5 working days upon instructions by GIZ’s Procurement Department. The cost of the sample is borne by the bidder. By submitting an offer, the supplier agrees that there is no additional charge for a sample of product to GIZ as a buyer. Upon completion of the technical evaluation, GIZ will inform suppliers when and where to pick up the samples. The samples must be in good condition and will be returned similarly after finalization of the evaluation. Financial Evaluation The financial evaluation will be done only in respect of those firms, which meet the eligibility criteria and the technical requirements. Offer must indicate the unit price of item and total price as per quantities given. Total amount of the price must be VAT exclusive, if applicable. Other conditions: Delivery place: The items will be delivered at Golf View Rise Building at Kacyiru-Gasabo, KG 563 St. Delivery period: the items must be delivered to GIZ within 14 days after signing confirmation of the order. Submission of the offer Please submit electronically your offer in PDF file to this email only: RW_Quotation@giz.deuntil latest 28.10.2026 You must write in your email subject this sentence: 7000025524 - Supply of Reusable Sanitary Pads without this sentence, your offer may not be considered. If the emails exceed the default email size of 30MB, offers can be exceptionally submitted through https://filetransfer.giz.de/ Offers submitted through any other sharing platform, as google documents or similar will not be considered. Hard copies are not allowed this time. GIZ Rwanda reserves all rights

description: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI) Title: SUPPLY OF MEDICAL CONSUMABLES Reference No: 018/G/EOI/2026/2027/RMS Date: 19/10/2026 1. Background Rwanda Medical Supply Ltd (RMS) is Rwanda’s central institution mandated to procure, store, and distribute medical commodities. In line with its strategic objective of improving access to high-quality health products and technologies, RMS seeks to expand its network of qualified manufacturers of medical consumables. RMS therefore invites eligible and qualified manufacturers to submit expressions of interest for the supply of medical consumables. 2. Scope of Supply Interested manufacturers may express interest in one or more of medical consumables listed in Annex 1. 3. Objectives This Expression of Interest aims to: Identify qualified manufacturers with the technical and operational capacity to supply the required products. Assess product availability, regulatory status, quality assurance, production capacity, lead times, and after-sales support. Develop a shortlist of eligible applicants for a subsequent competitive procurement process or other procurement method permitted under applicable procedures. 4. Eligibility Criteria Interested manufacturers must provide: A signed letter of expression of interest stating the line item(s) offered. A certificate of incorporation or business registration, together with evidence of authorization to manufacture, supply, or export the offered products. Product catalogues, instructions for use, and detailed technical data sheets demonstrating compliance with the specifications. Valid quality-management and product conformity documentation, as applicable, including ISO certificate/GMP and evidence of approval or registration by the relevant regulatory authority. Information on shelf life, storage conditions, packaging configuration, delivery lead time, and available technical support. 5. Submission Instructions Deadline for Submission of Expression of interest : You are requested to submit your expression of interest not later than 10 :00 AM, local time (8 :00 GMT), on 30/10/2026. Late submissions Will not be considered. Opened at RMS LTD board room on 30/10/ 2026 at 10 :30 AM, local time (8 :30 GMT). Expressions of interest must be submitted electronically to tenders@rms.rw. Requests for clarification may be submitted by email to rms.procurement@rms.rw, with copies to mimuragire@rms.rw and jbkageruka@rms.rw. Clarification requests must be received no later than halfway through the period allowed for submission of expressions of interest. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted for the next steps. title: Request for Proposal for Audit Services
raw_text: REF:117/CEO/KRK/26 Date: 15th October 2026 Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Request for proposal for Audit Services Kinazi Cassava Plant (KCP) Ltd is a cassava-processing factory located in Ruhango District, Southern Province of Rwanda; the factory produces fine cassava flour for human consumption and industrial use. Under this year of 2026, KCP is seeking to hire an audit firm to provide financial, compliance and value for money audit services for a year ending 31st December 2026, renewable for other 2 years subject to satisfactory performance of the assignment. KCP is now soliciting proposals (both technical and financial to be submitted separately in sealed envelopes) from qualified/Listed audit firms by both (iCPAR and RRA) for “Assurance Services to Provide Financial Audit Services to Kinazi Cassava Plant Ltd”. An acceptance of the best offer will be based on evaluation results of your proposals consistent with the criteria set out in this RFP, and in accordance with procurement regulations. Interested and qualified bidder should submit their proposals at the following address: Kinazi Cassava Plant, Chic building, 2nd floor. Attn. to: Chief Executive Officer, cc: Procurement Officer The successful Audit firm shall be endorsed and supervised by Office of Auditor General of State Finances. Kris R. KABALIRA Chief Executive Officer Kinazi Cassava Plant Ltd TERMS OF REFERENCE (ToR) Recruitment of an External Auditor Background Kinazi Cassava Plant ltd is a company operating in Rwanda. The organisation is seeking to recruit an independent and qualified external audit firm to conduct an annual audit of its financial statements and provide assurance on the accuracy, completeness and reliability of its financial reporting. Under the supervision of Auditor General of State Finances, the engagement will be undertaken in accordance with applicable laws and regulations of the Republic of Rwanda, International Standards on Auditing (ISA), the applicable financial reporting framework, and relevant requirements of the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Rwanda (ICPAR). Objective of the Assignment The overall objective is to appoint an independent external auditor to: Audit the organisation's annual financial statements. Express an independent professional opinion on whether the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position and financial performance of the organisation. Assess compliance with applicable accounting, tax and statutory requirements. Value for money Audit Review the adequacy of internal controls and financial management systems. Identify significant weaknesses, risks and areas requiring improvement. Provide practical recommendations to strengthen governance, financial management and internal controls. Scope of Work The external auditor shall conduct the audit in accordance with International Standards on Auditing and applicable Rwandan laws and regulations. The assignment shall include, but not be limited to: Financial Statements The auditor shall audit: Statement of financial position; Statement of income/expenditure or profit and loss; Statement of changes in equity; Statement of cash flows; Notes to the financial statements; and Supporting accounting records and schedules. Accounting and Internal Controls The auditor shall: Review the accounting systems and procedures; Assess key internal controls over income, expenditure, assets and liabilities; Review segregation of duties and authorisation procedures; Assess the adequacy of supporting documentation; Identify material control weaknesses and associated risks; and Recommend improvements where necessary. Compliance The auditor shall assess compliance, as applicable, with: Rwanda tax laws and regulations; Rwanda company and accounting legislation; Applicable employment and statutory requirements; The organisation's financial policies and procedures; and Other relevant laws and regulations. Verification The auditor shall undertake appropriate audit procedures, including: Examination of accounting records and supporting documents; Bank and cash verification; Review of assets and liabilities; Review of payroll and statutory deductions; Review of procurement and expenditure transactions; Verification of selected income and expenditure transactions; Review of related-party transactions, where applicable; and Other procedures considered necessary to form an audit opinion. Specific Responsibilities of the Auditor The appointed audit firm shall: Develop an appropriate audit plan and timetable. Conduct the audit objectively and independently. Obtain sufficient and appropriate audit evidence. Maintain appropriate audit working papers. Communicate significant audit findings promptly to management and/or the Board. Discuss identified weaknesses and proposed corrective actions with management. Issue an independent audit opinion. Prepare a management letter highlighting significant internal-control and financial-management issues. Follow up on recommendations from the previous audit Maintain confidentiality of all information obtained during the assignment. Deliverables The auditor shall provide the following deliverables: Audit planning memorandum/audit plan; Independent Auditor's Reports: Financial report Compliance report Value for money report Audited annual financial statements; Management Letter identifying significant findings and recommendations; Summary of internal-control weaknesses and recommended corrective actions; Any other report required by management, the Board or applicable legislation. Draft audit findings should be discussed with management before finalization of the audit report. Duration of the Assignment The audit is expected to cover the financial year ending 31 December 2026. The audit fieldwork is expected to commence in February 1st, 2027 and be completed by March 5th 2027, with the final audit report submitted no later than March 15th 2027. The engagement may be renewed subject to satisfactory performance, organisational requirements and applicable laws and regulations. Qualifications and Experience of the Audit Firm Interested audit firms should meet the following minimum requirements: Be legally registered and authorised to provide audit services in Rwanda. Be registered with the Institute of Certified Public Accountants of Rwanda (ICPAR) & RRA and hold valid practising credentials as required by applicable law. Demonstrate relevant experience in external/statutory audits. Have qualified and experienced audit personnel. Demonstrate experience auditing organisations of similar size and complexity. Demonstrate knowledge of Rwandan accounting, taxation and regulatory requirements. Have appropriate quality-control and audit procedures. Demonstrate independence and absence of conflicts of interest. Have adequate capacity and resources to complete the assignment within the required timeframe. Independence and Conflict of Interest The audit firm must be independent of the organization and must disclose any actual, potential or perceived conflict of interest. The auditor shall not undertake activities that compromise its independence or result in auditing its own work. The selected firm shall sign an independence and conflict-of-interest declaration before commencement of the assignment. Required Team The proposed team should include, at minimum: Engagement Partner/Lead Auditor; Audit Manager/Supervisor; and Qualified audit staff appropriate to the size and complexity of the assignment. The proposal should provide the names, qualifications, professional certifications and relevant experience of the proposed key personnel. Proposal Requirements Interested firms should submit a technical and financial proposal containing: Technical Proposal Company/firm profile; Certificate of registration and relevant licences; ICPAR registration/practising credentials; Understanding of the assignment; Proposed audit methodology and approach; Proposed work plan and timetable; Relevant experience and references; CVs of key personnel; Evidence of similar assignments undertaken; Independence and conflict-of-interest declaration; and At least three relevant client references, where available. Financial Proposal The financial proposal should clearly indicate: Professional audit fees; Applicable taxes; Any reimbursable expenses; Any other costs; and Total proposed cost. Financial proposal must be VAT inclusive All costs must be expressed in Rwandan currency Administrative required documents Valid tax clearance certificate Valid Social security clearance certificate audited financial statements Business licence Anti-fraud, corruption and conflicts of interest Confidentiality All information, documents and data obtained by the auditor during the assignment shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed to third parties without prior written authorisation, except where disclosure is required by law or professional obligations. Additional Requirements Bids must be prepared in English language No blacklisted company allowed to bid Kinazi cassava plant has rights to cancel tender in case there is clear reasons Bid validity period 120 days Evaluation Criteria KCP Ltd will evaluate all proposals based on the following criteria. To ensure consideration for this Request for Proposal, your proposal should be complete and include all of the following criteria: Administrative documents required: as highlighted here in Technical expertise and Overall Proposal Suitability: proposed solution(s) must meet the scope and needs included herein and be presented in a clear and organized manner, Bidders must provide audit plan and methodology, descriptions and documentation of staff technical expertise and experience. Bidders also need to provide their experiences as an organization which include but not limited to years of experiences, financial stability, expertise, and edge to other competitors. Technical proposal is evaluated at 70 % of total marks. Previous Work and Awards: Bidders will be evaluated on examples of their work pertaining to the requirement as well as client testimonials and references Value and Cost: Bidders will be evaluated on the cost of their solution(s) based on the work to be performed in accordance with the scope of this project. The financial proposal is evaluated at 30 % of total marks. Application Procedure Interested and eligible audit firms should submit their proposals to KCP Ltd office physical address at CHIC building, 2nd floor or on emails below not later than 9th, November/ 2026, 10:30 AM. Bids opening will take place at the same location on Monday 9th, November 2026, 11 AM. If you have any questions or require additional information, please do not hesitate to contact our procurement officer on Telephone: +250787833634 or by E-mail: jn.nitabaje@kcp.rw and info@kcp.rw.Late submissions will not be considered. Thank you for your time and consideration. We look forward to receiving your bids. Sincerely, Kris R. Kabalira Chief Executive Officer Kinazi Cassava Plant Ltd Attachment attachment_file_635a4692f2cf27e80cfc
