title: Request for Quotation (RFQ)_Supply and Delivery of Goats and Sheep for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project
raw_text: Project/Activity Name Heifer International Rwanda Agresso Work order: RW1338 Country: Rwanda Advertisement for Procurement Request for Quotation (RFQ) Supply and Delivery of Goats and Sheep for the Partnership for Resilient and Inclusive Small Livestock Markets (PRISM) Project. Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a Nonprofit and International Non-governmental Organization with the mission to alleviate hunger and poverty, while caring for the environment through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become theflagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. Heifer International Rwanda partners with smallholder farmers to build sustainable livelihoods by empowering them to use their own energy, ingenuity, and dreams to fuel their success out of hunger and poverty. Heifer programs mobilize communities and foster the organization of associations, cooperatives and social networks while strengthening their capacity to address development challenges. Purpose and Objective The objective of this procurement is to obtain the required quantities of livestock, meeting the prescribed technical and quality standards, and to deliver them to the designated locations in Rwanda’s Northern, Southern, and Western Provinces. How to Apply Detailed request for Quotation (RFQ) is attached below. All registered and interested companies are requested to submit their proposals, marked with clear subject line: “Supply and Delivery of Goats and Sheep for PRISM Project” to procurement-rw@heifer.org not later than 29th October2026 at 5.00pm Kigali time. Done on October 5th, 2026. Heifer International Rwanda Management Attachment attachment_file_d72cd36e7eeee94955bc

Tenders submitted without evidence of payment will be automatically rejected. 4. TENDER PUBLICATION DATE October 16,2026 SUBMISSION DEADLINE October 28,2026, at 11:00AM SITE VISIT DATE &TIME Wednesday, October 21,2026 and Friday October 23,206 At Kicukiro Niboye near DUHAMI-ADRI Headquarters From 09:00AM to 12:00PM SITE VISIT CONTACT 0788305329 SUBMISSION LOCATION DUHAMIC-ADRI Head Office, Kicukiro-Niboye (Only hard copy submissions are accepted) INQUIRY CONTACT EMAIL procurement@duhamic.org.rw 1. Brief description of DUHAMIC-ADRI DUHAMIC-ADRI is a local Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) based in Kigali, Rwanda, established and legally recognized under Ministerial Order No. 943/05 of 12 July 1985. The organization operates in compliance with the applicable laws and regulations of Rwanda, including Law No. 058/2024 of 20 June 2024, governing non-governmental organizations. Vision A rural world responsible for its self-socio-economic development. Mission Supporting integrated initiatives for the holistic development of rural population in their struggle for self-reliance. Objective The Objective of the Organization is sustainable economic self-development of rural populations through strengthened community structures, capacity building, and integrated support services. Strategic Pillars Livelihoods and economic capacity development Environment protection and conservation Mobilization for social change and family promotion DUHAMIC-ADRI organizational sustainability 2. title: Tender Notice for Provision of Migration Services for Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 and Mac Device Management
raw_text: SUSTAINABLE GROWERS RWANDA P.O BOX 864 Kigali, Rwanda INVITATION TO BID Title of Tender: Provision of Migration Services for Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 and Mac Device ManagementTender Reference Number: MSGWS/10/2026 Procurement Method: Open Tender Date of Issue: 13 October 2026 Submission Deadline: 23 October 2026 at 5:00 PM (17h00) Kigali time I. Introduction Sustainable Growers Rwanda (SGR) is a non-governmental organization that specializes in innovative coffee cultivation training for smallholder women coffee farmers, with the goal of increasing their visibility in the coffee supply chain. Supported by Bloomberg Philanthropies and the governments of Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of Congo and Tanzania, SGR has reached over 77,000 women farmers and over 341,000 family members. SGR currently runs on Google Workspace and uses Apple MacBooks exclusively. It intends to move to Microsoft 365 Business Premium and adopt cloud-native identity and device management through Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft Intune. SGR has approximately 19 users and will not deploy or maintain any on-premises infrastructure. SGR is therefore seeking a qualified Microsoft partner to plan and deliver the migration, configure the tenant and its security baseline, bring the MacBook estate under management, and hand over a documented environment that the SGR IT Manager can operate independently. II. General Qualifications and Required Documents The objective of this tender is to identify a professional, experienced firm to deliver a complete Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 migration and Mac device management implementation for SGR. 1. Administrative documents (mandatory, pass/fail) Registration certificate from RDB Valid tax clearance certificate from Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) Valid social security clearance certificate from RSSB, if applicable Confirmation that the bidder has an Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) Evidence of current Microsoft Partner status (e.g. Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program listing or partner ID) At least three (3) completed Microsoft 365 migration or configuration projects; at least one should include migration from Google Workspace or another non-Microsoft platform Demonstrated experience managing Apple macOS devices through Microsoft Intune, with at least one reference. Administrative requirements for international bidders. This tender is open to qualified national and international firms. In place of items 1 to 4 above, international bidders must submit valid company registration documents and equivalent tax compliance certificates or other applicable statutory documents issued by the competent authorities in their country of establishment, subject to SGR’s verification and acceptance. 2. Pricing instructions All prices must be quoted in Rwandan Francs (RWF), with VAT shown separately and included in the total. International bidders must convert their prices into RWF and state the exchange rate and date used. Migration and implementation services must be quoted at standard commercial rates and itemized separately from any Microsoft licensing costs. Any optional item, assumption or exclusion must be stated separately. SGR will not accept unapproved hidden or post-award charges. Prices shall not change for the duration of the contract. Pricing and withholding taxes. International bidders shall ensure that their financial quotations take into account all applicable taxes and statutory deductions under Rwandan law, including withholding taxes (WHT). Where applicable, withholding tax shall be deducted and remitted to the Rwanda Revenue Authority in accordance with the law. Bidders should factor this tax treatment into their quoted prices, as withholding tax shall not constitute an additional payment over and above the accepted contract price. III. Terms of Reference 1. Objectives The objective of this assignment is to contract a qualified service provider to: Migrate SGR from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365 Business Premium without permanent loss of mail, calendar or file data. Establish Microsoft Entra ID as the primary identity platform for all users and connected applications. Implement Microsoft Intune for management of all SGR macOS devices. Configure Microsoft security and compliance baseline controls, including MFA, Conditional Access, self-service password reset and Microsoft Defender for Business. Migrate Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive content to Exchange Online, OneDrive and SharePoint Online, validated against an agreed test plan. Create Apple Business Manager (ABM), integrate it with Entra ID and Intune, and recommend a future device procurement and enrolment path. Provide knowledge transfer, administrator training and documentation so the SGR IT Manager can run the environment after handover. 2. Current Environment and Target State Figures below are estimates. The selected provider must measure and confirm them during discovery. Area Current Target Users Approximately 19 Approximately 19 on Microsoft 365 Business Premium (nonprofit) Identity Google Workspace accounts Microsoft Entra ID Mail and calendar Gmail, Google Calendar Exchange Online with Outlook Files Google Drive OneDrive and SharePoint Online Meetings and chat Google Meet Microsoft Teams Devices Approximately 20 Apple MacBooks from multiple vendors, not centrally managed Same devices enrolled and managed in Intune Endpoint protection Not centrally managed Microsoft Defender for Business Device procurement Mixed vendors, no central enrolment Apple Business Manager linked to Intune On-premises infrastructure None None, and none planned Data to migrate Approximately 1.2 TB (Gmail and Google Drive combined) Migrated and validated in Microsoft 365 3. Scope of Work The selected provider shall deliver the following services. Bidders may propose their own phasing, but every item below must be covered. 3.1 Assessment and discovery Audit the Google Workspace tenant: users, groups, aliases, delegated access, service accounts, shared drives, sharing permissions and external links, calendar resources and shared calendars. Measure actual mail and Drive volumes per user and per shared drive, rather than relying on the 1.2 TB estimate. Identify all third-party services that use "Sign in with Google" or integrate with Google Workspace, and propose how each will authenticate after migration. Inventory every MacBook: model, chipset, macOS version, purchase source, serial number and Apple Business Manager eligibility. Review domains, DNS hosting and current MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records. Produce a migration plan and risk assessment, including migration tooling, data mapping, pre-stage and delta sync approach, cutover runbook, rollback plan with go/no-go criteria, and an end-user communication plan. 3.2 Microsoft 365 tenant configuration Configure Entra ID: domains, users, groups, roles and group-based licensing. Enforce multi-factor authentication (Microsoft Authenticator) for all users and configure self-service password reset. Create and document break-glass emergency access accounts and apply a least-privilege administrator model. Build Conditional Access policies (MFA, block legacy authentication, compliant-device requirement), tested in report-only mode before enforcement. Apply Microsoft-recommended security baselines and Exchange Online protection (anti-spam, anti-phishing, Safe Links, malware). Configure baseline Microsoft Purview controls: starting sensitivity labels, data loss prevention rules and retention policies. 3.3 Google Workspace migration Migrate Gmail to Exchange Online, Google Calendar to Outlook, and Google Drive and shared drives to OneDrive and SharePoint Online. Agree how Google-native files (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Sites, Apps Script) will be converted or handled as exceptions. Run a pilot with the IT Manager and a small user group before production migration. Pre-stage bulk data ahead of cutover so the go-live weekend carries only the final delta sync, DNS change and validation. Execute the cutover over a single weekend and validate mail flow, calendar integrity, file access, permissions and sign-in against the agreed test plan. Provide on-site support on the first business day after cutover. 3.4 Microsoft Teams deployment Configure team and channel structure, meeting, messaging and calling policies, external and guest access, and collaboration settings. 3.5 Microsoft Intune implementation Configure macOS enrolment (Company Portal and Automated Device Enrolment where eligible). Deploy compliance policies (OS version, FileVault, firewall, password) and configuration profiles. Enable FileVault encryption with recovery key escrow and a software update policy. Deploy Microsoft 365 apps and agreed business applications. Enrol and validate all approximately 20 MacBooks, securing business data before any device reset. 3.6 Microsoft Defender for Business Onboard all enrolled devices through Intune and configure next-generation protection, attack surface reduction, alerting and reporting. Connect device risk signals to Conditional Access. 3.7 Apple Business Manager assessment and setup Create or verify the ABM account, complete Apple organization verification, and link ABM to Intune and Entra ID. Configure Automated Device Enrolment profiles and the Apps and Books token. Document per-device eligibility and recommend a future procurement path so new MacBooks enrol automatically. 3.8 Knowledge transfer and documentation Involve the SGR IT Manager throughout configuration. Deliver hands-on administrator training covering the admin center, Entra ID, Exchange Online, Intune, ABM and Defender. Deliver a short end-user readiness session with a written guide before cutover. Produce as-built documentation, an administrator runbook (including joiner and leaver procedures), support procedures and a handover report. 3.9 Post-go-live support Provide 30 days of included support from handover, covering defects, migration follow-up, enrolment issues and IT Manager assistance. Propose optional support arrangements beyond the 30 days, priced separately. 4. Deliverables Each deliverable will be accepted by SGR against the criteria below. Migration acceptance is a separate, explicit sign-off after post-cutover validation. # Deliverable Acceptance criteria D1 Discovery and assessment report Complete inventory of users, groups, shared drives, third-party integrations and devices, with measured data volumes and rated risks D2 Migration plan and implementation schedule Approved by SGR; includes data mapping, cutover runbook, test plan, rollback triggers and communication plan D3 Configured Microsoft 365 tenant Entra ID licensed; all users registered for MFA; SSPR live; break-glass accounts documented; Conditional Access enforced with no unintended lockouts D4 Exchange Online implementation Mail flow tested inbound and outbound; SPF, DKIM and DMARC configured; protection policies applied D5 Teams implementation Teams, channels and policies deployed; meetings, chat and external access tested D6 Intune implementation Enrolment, compliance and configuration profiles deployed and validated on pilot devices D7 macOS device enrolment and management All in-scope MacBooks enrolled, FileVault enabled with keys escrowed, every device compliant D8 Microsoft Defender for Business implementation All enrolled devices onboarded and reporting; alerting configured; no unresolved high-severity alerts at handover D9 Apple Business Manager setup and recommendations ABM created and linked to Intune; enrolment profile configured; per-device eligibility and procurement recommendations documented D10 Google Workspace data migration Mail, calendar and Drive content migrated and validated; exceptions logged and accepted by SGR D11 IT Manager training Training delivered and signed off by the SGR IT Manager; sessions recorded on request D12 As-built documentation and support procedures Configuration documents, administrator runbook and end-user guide reviewed and accepted by SGR D13 Project handover report Handover session completed; open items listed with owners and dates D14 30 days post-go-live support Support delivered from handover date, closed with a review of Secure Score, device compliance and open items 5. Timeline and Migration Approach The assignment should be completed within a maximum of six (6) weeks from contract signing, followed by 30 days of post-go-live support. Bidders must submit a detailed work plan; the phasing below is indicative. Phase Key activities Indicative duration 1. Discovery and migration design Google Workspace audit, device inventory, migration and rollback plan, SGR sign-off Week 1 2. Tenant build and security baseline Entra ID, MFA, Conditional Access (report-only), Exchange, Teams, SharePoint, Intune, Defender, ABM, Purview Weeks 2 to 3 3. Pilot, data migration and cutover Pilot group, bulk data pre-stage, device enrolment, cutover weekend, day-one support Weeks 4 4. Stabilization and handover Monitoring and tuning, residual items, training, documentation, handover Weeks 5 to 6 The approach must respect these principles: Build alongside, then switch. The Microsoft 365 tenant is configured and tested while staff keep working in Google Workspace. Single-weekend cutover. The production cutover happens over one weekend, on a date approved by SGR that avoids month-end, audits and major events. Phase gates. No phase starts until SGR signs off the previous one; no user data moves before the tenant is accepted. Defined rollback. A written rollback plan with go/no-go criteria is agreed and tested before go-live. Google Workspace retained. Google Workspace stays licensed and available until SGR formally accepts the migration. 6. SGR Responsibilities SGR will provide: Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 administrator access for the duration of the project. Access to DNS hosting, or a person able to make DNS changes during the cutover window. Confirmation that Microsoft 365 Business Premium nonprofit licences are active and sufficient. SGR's D-U-N-S number and an authorized contact for Apple Business Manager verification. Two to three pilot users, and access to all MacBooks for scheduled enrolment. Timely decisions and sign-offs within the turnaround agreed at kick-off. 7. Out of Scope On-premises infrastructure deployment, configuration or management. Windows device management (the estate is macOS only). Custom application development, including rebuilding Google Apps Script automations. 8. Key Personnel The bidder must propose a team with, at minimum: Role Minimum qualification Minimum experience Lead consultant / project lead Degree in IT, computer science or related field; Microsoft 365 Administrator Expert or equivalent 7 years, including at least 2 Microsoft 365 migrations as lead Endpoint engineer Microsoft Certified: Endpoint Administrator Associate or equivalent; Apple/macOS management experience 3 years in system administration and device management Security engineer Relevant Microsoft security or identity certification (e.g. SC-300, SC-200) 3 years in system administration or security operations 9. Technical Proposal Requirements Company profile, registration documents and Microsoft Partner evidence Understanding of the assignment and proposed methodology Detailed work plan and timeline, including the proposed cutover weekend approach Proposed migration tooling and how it handles the 1.2 TB volume, Google API throttling and Google-native file conversion Rollback plan with go/no-go criteria Proposed security baseline, mapped to Microsoft recommendations or the CIS Critical Security Controls, stating any controls not covered Approach to enrolling existing MacBooks not eligible for Automated Device Enrolment Training and knowledge transfer plan Risk register with mitigations Assumptions and SGR responsibilities Post-implementation support options beyond the included 30 days Team composition, CVs and certifications 10. Financial Proposal Requirements The financial proposal must be submitted in RWF and must show: Section Content required A. Migration and implementation services Itemized by phase or service area, at standard commercial rates B. 30-day post-go-live support Confirmed as included, or priced if not C. Optional items Each optional item (Section 7) priced separately The bidder must also state the quotation validity period and proposed payment terms. 11. Evaluation Criteria Criterion Weight Methodology, work plan, cutover and rollback approach 25% Experience with similar Microsoft 365 migrations and macOS management (references) 20% Qualifications and certifications of key personnel 15% Security baseline, training and knowledge transfer plan 10% Pricing competitiveness and transparency 25% Experience with NGOs or the development sector 5% IV. Standard Provisions Guidelines, policies and ethics. All bidders must commit to the SGR Procurement Procedures Manual, the SGR Anti-terrorism and Anti-money Laundering Policy, and the SGR Anti-fraud, Bribery and Corruption Policy. Conflict of interest and disqualification. Bidders shall disclose any relationship with SGR staff and shall not submit more than one bid. SGR will disqualify any bidder that attempts to influence the process improperly, colludes with other bidders, engages in bribery, is blacklisted by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or SGR, has corruption-related convictions, unresolved contract disputes or is in bankruptcy proceedings. Bids received late, incomplete, with unsigned handwritten amendments, or with misleading information will also be disqualified. Data protection and confidentiality. The selected provider will have administrative access to SGR systems and data. It must sign a confidentiality and data processing agreement, comply with Rwanda's Law No. 058/2021 on the protection of personal data and privacy, use access only for this assignment, and return or remove all credentials and data at handover. Evaluation and award. The contract will be awarded through quality and cost-based selection to the responsive bidder with the highest combined score. SGR may request clarifications, a presentation of the proposed approach, or negotiate with any bidder before award. Withdrawal. SGR reserves the right to withdraw this tender at any time without notice or liability, and to accept or reject any bid without giving reasons. Tender costs. Bidders bear all costs of preparing their bid, whether or not successful. Notification of award. All bidders will receive formal notification of the outcome. Bid validity. Bids shall remain valid for 60 days from the submission deadline. V. Guideline for Bid Submission Interested and qualified firms must submit separate technical and financial proposals electronically to recruitment@sustainablegrowers.org not later than 23 October 2026 at 5:00 PM (17h00) local time. Late bids will be automatically rejected. Questions may be sent to the same address no later than 21 October 2026 at 5:00 PM (17h00) local time. Only written answers issued by SGR are official; verbal information from SGR staff is not binding. SGR may request further information from any bidder, and failure to respond by the stated deadline may lead to disqualification. Done at Kigali, on 13 October 2026 Christine Condo Chief Executive Officer, Sustainable Growers

title: Prequalification of Suppliers and Update of the Food, Goods & Services Vendor Roster
raw_text: 29 September 2026 PREQUALIFICATION OF SUPPLIERS AND UPDATE OF THE FOOD, GOODS & SERVICES VENDOR ROSTER EOI number: RWA26NF005 A. Background 1. The United Nations World Food Programme hereinafter referred to as the “WFP”, with its Headquarters located in Via C.G. Viola, 68/70, 00148 Rome, Italy is the leading humanitarian organization saving lives and changing lives, delivering food assistance in emergencies and working with communities to improve nutrition and build resilience by assisting almost 100 million people in around 83 countries each year. 2. The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), Rwanda Country Office, invites qualified and experienced companies to submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) for prequalification and possible inclusion in its Food, Goods and Services Vendor Roster. This exercise is intended to broaden WFP Rwanda’s supplier base, attract new and capable market participants, align the roster with the current WFP procurement taxonomy, and update the information and continued interest of suppliers already included in the roster. 3. IMPORTANT FOR CURRENT ROSTER SUPPLIERS Existing suppliers that have not responded to WFP Rwanda solicitation invitations during the period from 1 January 2026 to the date of this EOI are required to re-apply if they wish to remain under consideration for future procurement opportunities. Existing suppliers whose company information, ownership, contacts, legal documents, banking details, capacity, or service offering has changed are also required to respond and submit updated information. A current roster entry does not constitute automatic confirmation or renewal. B. Categories Covered by the EOI Suppliers may apply under the WFP procurement taxonomy shown in Annex 1. Applicants must select the category or categories that accurately reflect their demonstrated legal mandate, technical capacity, experience, staffing, equipment, and financial capability. A supplier may apply for a maximum of TWO (2) Level 3 categories across the entire EOI C. Mandatory Cover Letter Instructions The signed cover letter must clearly state: the applicant’s full legal name and registration number; whether the applicant is a new supplier or is already included in the WFP Rwanda vendor roster; the exact taxonomy selection for each application: Level 1 category, Level 2 category, and Level 3 category; a maximum of two Level 3 categories for which the supplier seeks prequalification; a brief explanation of the supplier’s relevant capability and experience for each selected category; and the name, title, telephone number, and email address of the authorized focal point. Applications that do not clearly identify the selected category or that apply for more than two categories may be considered non-compliant. D. Eligibility and Minimum Qualification Criteria Legally registered and authorized to operate in the relevant field. Valid tax registration and tax compliance status. Demonstrated relevant experience in each category applied for. Adequate technical capacity, qualified personnel, equipment, systems, and operational capability. Adequate financial capacity to perform potential contracts. Ability to comply with applicable WFP contractual, ethical, safeguarding, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, sanctions, health, safety, environmental, and quality requirements. No conflict of interest that would compromise participation in a WFP procurement process. E. Submission Requirements Signed cover letter meeting Section 3 requirements. Completed supplier information form, including legal name, physical address, contacts, ownership, and authorized representative. Valid certificate of registration/incorporation and relevant operating licences. Valid tax registration and tax clearance/compliance certificate. Company profile describing core business, years of operation, staffing, facilities, equipment, geographic coverage, and organizational structure. Evidence of relevant experience for each category applied for, such as contracts, purchase orders, completion certificates, or client reference letters. Audited financial statements for the most recent three financial years, or acceptable alternative evidence where audited statements are not legally required, subject to WFP review. Current bank details and bank reference letter, where requested during due diligence. UNGM registration number, if available. Suppliers not yet registered may be requested to register at a later stage. For existing roster suppliers, a declaration confirming whether company information remains unchanged or identifying all updates since the last submission. All supporting documentation listed above shall be prepared in accordance with the instructions provided in the EOI and submitted via email to rwa.procurement@wfp.org referencing the subject ‘’Response to EOI ref. No RWA26NF005’’. The deadline for response to this request for EOI: (Friday, 31st October 2026, 1700hrs, Kigali Time) WFP will not consider incomplete or unsigned submissions. All responses and supporting documentation received will be treated as strictly confidential and will not be made available to the public. This request for EOI does not constitute a solicitation. WFP reserves the right to change or cancel this procurement process or any of its requirements at any time during the process; any such action will be communicated to all participants. Should you have any questions please do not hesitate to contact us at rwa.procurement@wfp.org. Evaluation Process: After the deadline for submission of responses has passed, WFP will evaluate responses received and will notify eligible participants of the outcome of the evaluation. Eligible suppliers will be invited to participate in the bidding process for the proposed tender. Sincerely, _________________________________ Hien ADJEMIAN Head of Supply Chain World Food Programme, Rwanda Attachment attachment_file_882a73a53ccfcdc524ec attachment_file_0073e1d4aebf3fa62fde

title: Tender Notice for Supply and Delivery of Closed-System Transfer Devices (CSTDS) for Safe Chemotherapy Handling for Butaro Cancer Center of Excellence
raw_text: PUBLIC TENDER NOTICE # PIH/IMB/10919/M09/FY27 TENDER TITTLE: SUPPLY AND DELIVERY OF CLOSED-SYSTEM TRANSFER DEVICES (CSTDS) FOR SAFE CHEMOTHERAPY HANDLING FOR BUTARO CANCER CENTER OF EXCELLENCE. SOURCING METHOD: OPEN COMPETITION FOR DOMESTIC COMPANIES. Partners In Health (PIH) is a nonprofit organization with its headquarters in Boston, Massachusetts, whose mission is to provide quality health care for poor and most in need populations around the world. Since 2005, the Ministry of Health in Rwanda has worked with PIH Rwanda, also known as Inshuti Mu Buzima, to improve the quality of care in the country and increase health care access for Rwanda most in need populations. PIH/IMB have since helped to bring high-quality health care to three Districts namely: Kayonza, Burera and Kirehe. Partners In Health / Inshuti Mu Buzima is seeking proposals from qualified and authorized medical companies for Supply of Closed-System Transfer Devices (CSTDs) for Safe Chemotherapy Handling for Butaro Cancer Center of Excellence as per term of reference (ToRs) found in annex. Interested and qualified bidders should provide their proposals bearing the following requirements: I. BIDDERS/ VENDORS ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA The bidders falling in any of the following categories will be ineligible to participate in this tender and / or its award: The Bidder should not be suspended or blacklisted by PIH-IMB or OnePIH nor blacklisted or revoked licenses by the Rwanda Public Procurement Authority or other relevant regulatory bodies. The Bidder should not have any ongoing contracts with PIH-IMB that demonstrates poor performance. Vendors or Companies owner must not be employed by PIH or One PIH within five past years, unless PIH seeks their expertise for consultancy services based on proven specialized knowledge. Any bidder that owns operates, or exercises controlling shareholding in more than one company is strictly prohibited from submitting more than one bid under this tender. Submission of multiple bids by related or affiliated entities under the same beneficial ownership shall constitute a breach of tender participation rules. NB: Non-compliance with any of above provision shall result in the annulment of bid examination process/ tender competition. II. COMPULSORY REQUIREMENTS: a. The Bidder shall submit Company profile including company name; location details, showing a well-known physical address building; Street number Emails, contacts. b. Bid Security Requirements: The Bidders must submit a bid security based on the value of their financial proposal, as follows: For financial proposals ≥ RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.1%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 950,000,001 to RWF 1,000,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 0.5%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 500,000,001 to RWF 950,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.0%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 100,000,001 to RWF 500,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 1.5%. For financial proposals ranging from RWF 20,000,001 to RWF 100,000,000, the bidder shall submit a bid security equal to 2.0%. No bid security is required for financial proposals with a value of ≤ RWF 20,000,000. III. ADMINISTRATIVE REQUIREMENT: The Bidder shall submit registration of domestic company issued by RDB in the same domain required. The Bidder shall submit valid RRA tax clearance. IV. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS: Bidders should consider ToRs especially for section 9 and 10 available in Partners In Health/Inshuti Mu Buzima e-Procurement System following this link: (https://pih-imb.org.rw/eprocurement/index.php) v. FINANCIALLY, THE BID SHALL INDICATE: A commitment letter for the submission of the Performance Security (Bank Guarantee). The letter shall state that, if awarded, the bidder will provide a Performance Security (Bank Guarantee) prior to signing the contract. The Performance Security shall depend on the contract value, as follows: 5% of the contract whose value exceeds FRW 500,000,000; 6% of the contract value between FRW 100,000,000 FRW to FRW 500,000,000; 7% of the contract value between FRW 50,000,000 to FRW 100,000,000; 10% of the contract price whose value is between FRW 20,000,001 to FRW 50,000,000. The performance security is not required for contracts valued at or below FRW 20,000,000. The financial proposal shall be submitted in Rwandan Francs currency. The financial proposal shall include all applicable taxes and charges. The financial proposal shall include terms and conditions of payment (preferably after execution of project). The proposal should indicate the shortest execution period. The financial proposal validity shall not be lower than 120 calendar days from the day of its submission to PIH. VI. INCOTERMS:DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) at Kayonza IMB office (Rwinkwavu warehouse) VII. title: Tender Notice for Construction of Two Classrooms for a TVET Facility
raw_text: U’MWIZA-RWANDA/UNBOUND PROJECT INVITATION TO BID / TENDER DOCUMENT CONSTRUCTION OF TWO CLASSROOMS FOR A TVET FACILITY Gasabo District, Rusororo Sector, Kigali City, Rwanda 1. Background of U’Mwiza-Rwanda and project introduction U’Mwiza-Rwanda, in collaboration with the Government of Rwanda, implements community-based initiatives aimed at addressing key challenges affecting vulnerable children, youth, families and communities. Through its collaboration with relevant government institutions and local authorities, U’Mwiza-Rwanda supports initiatives that promote access to education, skills development, social inclusion and opportunities for vulnerable community members to improve their livelihoods through implementing initiatives that respond to identified community needs. As part of these efforts, U’Mwiza/Unbound Rwanda project is implementing a Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) initiative in Gasabo District, Rusororo Sector, Kigali City, with outreach to young people from Rusororo and Bumbogo sectors. The initiative responds to the limited access to affordable vocational training opportunities available to vulnerable and out-of-school youth in the area. The project specifically targets youth aged between 15 and 30, including school dropouts, economically vulnerable young people, young women and other disadvantaged groups who face barriers to accessing skills development opportunities. The TVET initiative is designed to provide practical and market-oriented training in tailoring and masonry, combining technical skills with mentorship and basic entrepreneurship training. Approximately 150 young people are expected to be trained and graduate each year through the program. The project seeks to equip young people with practical skills that can increase their opportunities for employment, self-employment and income generation. The need for the project has been identified through consultations with community members, local leaders and government representatives, together with observations and community feedback regarding unemployment, school dropout and the absence of accessible TVET facilities in the area. To respond to these needs, U’Mwiza/Unbound Rwanda Project is supporting the construction of two classrooms that will form part of the TVET training facility. Each classroom will measure approximately 8 metres by 7 metres, providing approximately 56 m² of floor space, with an internal height of 5.30 metres. The classrooms are intended to provide a safe, functional, durable and conducive learning environment for practical and vocational training. Accordingly, U’Mwiza/Unbound Rwanda invites qualified and competent construction contractors to submit bids for the construction of the two TVET classrooms. 2. Project information Procuring/Implementing organization U’Mwiza–Rwanda Project Project Construction of Two TVET Classrooms Location Gasabo District, Rusororo Sector, Kigali City, Rwanda Target beneficiaries Vulnerable and out-of-school youth aged 15–30 from Rusororo and Bumbogo sectors Number of classrooms 2 Approximate size 8 m × 7 m per classroom (approximately 56 m² each; 112 m² total floor area) Internal height 5.30 m from finished floor level to underside of roof structure 3. Contractor’s responsibilities The selected contractor shall be responsible for organizing and executing the works within the agreed implementation schedule, providing competent labour and workmanship, supplying the required construction materials and equipment within the agreed scope, maintaining site safety, protecting completed works, coordinating technical supervision, correcting defects identified during inspection, and completing the works in accordance with the approved design and specifications. 4. Required bid information To facilitate technical and financial evaluation, bidders should provide the following information: Company profile and evidence of relevant construction experience. Relevant experience in construction of school, TVET or comparable public/institutional buildings, where available. Proposed work methodology and implementation schedule. Details of proposed technical personnel and supervision arrangements. Detailed financial quotation/BOQ covering the full scope of works. Evidence of legal registration and any applicable construction/professional authorizations required under Rwandan regulations. Having insurance for man powers from any insurance company Any assumptions, exclusions or proposed alternatives, clearly identified. Contact details of the bidder and authorized representative. 5. Handover requirements Before final handover, the contractor shall ensure that the classrooms and associated works are complete, clean and ready for use; electrical and water systems have been tested; identified defects have been rectified; safety and accessibility features are in place; and all completed works conform to the approved design and technical specifications. 6. Bidding period Any interested bidder must send his/her application to rwanda@intl.unbound.org within 7 working days respectively from 20th October 2026 up to 26TH October 2026 at 10h00 AM. The attached documents are the terms of reference including the class drawings and the bill of quantities (BOQ). Background Rwanda Medical Supply Ltd (RMS) is Rwanda’s central institution mandated to procure, store, and distribute medical commodities. In line with its strategic objective of improving access to high-quality health products and technologies, RMS seeks to expand its network of qualified manufacturers and authorized suppliers of medical consumables. RMS therefore invites eligible and qualified manufacturers and authorized suppliers to submit expressions of interest for the supply and delivery of rapid tests. 2. Scope of Supply Interested manufacturers may express interest in one or more of the rapid-test line items listed in Annex 1. Rapid tests for qualitative detection of specified antigens, antibodies, or clinical analytes. Urine dipsticks for ten-parameter urinalysis. 3. Objectives This Expression of Interest aims to: Identify qualified manufacturers with the technical and operational capacity to supply the required products. Assess product availability, regulatory status, quality assurance, production capacity, lead times, and after-sales support. Develop a shortlist of eligible applicants for a subsequent competitive procurement process or other procurement method permitted under applicable procedures. 4. Eligibility Criteria Interested manufacturers must provide: A signed letter of expression of interest stating the line item(s) offered. Upon notification and before contract signing, the three lowest evaluated bidders will be required to submit product samples to Rwanda Medical Supply Ltd (RMS), KN 8 Avenue, Kacyiru, Gasabo District, Kigali City, P.O. Box 640, Kigali, Rwanda. A certificate of incorporation or business registration, together with evidence of authorization to manufacture, supply, or export the offered products. Product catalogues, instructions for use, and detailed technical data sheets demonstrating compliance with the specifications. Valid quality-management and product conformity documentation, as applicable, including ISO 13485 and evidence of approval or registration by the relevant regulatory authority. Information on shelf life, storage conditions, packaging configuration, delivery lead time, and available technical support. 5. Submission Instructions Expressions of interest must be submitted electronically to tenders@rms.rw. The submission deadline is 4 November 2026. Requests for clarification may be submitted by email to rms.procurement@rms.rw, with copies to vhigiro@rms.rw and jbkageruka@rms.rw. Clarification requests must be received no later than halfway through the period allowed for submission of expressions of interest. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted for the next steps. Kit 2 Toxoplasma gondii IgG and IgM Antibody Test Toxoplasma gondii IgG and IgM antibody test. Kit 4 Helicobacter pylori Antigen in Stool Rapid Test Rapid cassette or strip for qualitative detection of H. pylori antigen in human stool. raw_text: TENDER NOTICE Tender title: Hiring Individual Consultant to conduct a Baseline survey for Tegura Ejo (EduCare) Project Procurement Method: Individual Consultancy Tender Ref no: 025/SOS-CV/NCB/CS/2026 CLIENT: SOS CHILDREN’S VILLAGES RWANDA The Tegura Ejo (EduCare) Project (2026–2029) is an integrated, child-centred, systems-strengthening initiative implemented by SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda in partnership with relevant Government institutions and community stakeholders (IZUs, child protection actors and more, as indicated in the project reach and categories) across Musanze, Huye, and Nyamagabe Districts, and with SOS Children’s Villages Denmark. Tegura Ejo takes point of departure in the evidence, achievements and lessons learned from the Kura Umenye Project, which includes comprehensive baseline, midterm, and final evaluations, a sustainability assessment, and consistent monitoring data. Tegura Ejo responds to the recognition that children’s educational outcomes cannot be sustainably improved through classroom-based interventions alone; rather, learning is shaped by the interaction of household economic conditions, parenting practices, psychosocial wellbeing, school environments and the availability of responsive community and institutional support. SOS CHILDREN’S VILLAGES RWANDA hereby invites Individuals who are qualified to express the interest in conducting a baseline survey for Tegura Ejo (EduCare) Project. Participation is open on equal conditions to all individuals specialized in the field. The individuals must be registered with Rwanda Development Board and should not be on the blacklist recorded of any recognized national or international Institution. title: Tender for 14 Senior Software Engineering Trainers for Code Reviews (Local Expert Positions) as Trainers for the Rwandan Software Development Trainee Program "1000 Intermediate Developers"
raw_text: Tender for 14 Senior Software Engineering Trainers for Code Reviews (Local Expert Positions) as Trainers for the Rwandan Software Development Trainee Program "1000 Intermediate Developers" 1. General information 1.1 About KB21 KB21 Ltd. is committed to promoting the Rwandan IT scene. We focus on capacity developmentand job creation in the Rwandan IT economy. KB21 Ltd. has been partnering with Rwandan companies, institutions, and individual trainers in several projects, connecting Rwandan tech teams to international projects and remote work opportunities. In 2019, we introduced our independent training program, called “The Gym”, together with our partner Tech in Ruanda e.V., guiding young Rwandan ICT talent through a structured set of technology and professional skills modules empowering them to provide services for global clients. Later this program evolved into the “1000 Intermediate developers” program. 1.2 About "The Gym" and "1000 intermediate developers" The Gym is Rwanda's most intense software development trainee program. Trainees join the program with solid foundations in software development and undergo a rigorous 6-month, full-time, on-site training in software development, professional skills and ways of work that brings them to the level of being able to join international software development teams as Junior Developers. The 1000 intermediate developers program adapts The Gym’s 6-month full-time training into a 12-month part-time program that runs in parallel to university, targeting students at the beginning of their studies. After completion of the 12-month core training, successful graduates transition into the project phase of their traineeship, which lasts until graduation from university. The project-phase allows participants to grow to the level of intermediate software developers. Graduates of The Gym work remotely from Rwanda for international companies. Find out more on https://www.thegym-rwanda.com/ For this assignment: We are looking for 14 senior software engineering trainers to provide specialized support for code reviews and one-on-one technical coaching for our trainees. The experts need to have extensive experience as software developers, including working in advanced roles on international projects, and should have prior experience coaching junior developers and acting as trainers. They should be skilled in conducting code reviews, providing detailed feedback on participants’ mistakes, and guiding their technology skill development. At the same time, the experts should be able to deliver focused, individualized technical coaching sessions to participants, helping them overcome challenges and improve their proficiency in specific technologies 2. Contractual information The service can be performed remotely. The service performance period is November 2026 to January 2027. The legal entity that is carrier of The Gym and 1000 intermediate developers is KB21 Ltd., a Rwandan limited liability company. Quotes for this tender can be specified in EUR or in RWF. Companies need to specify the individual trainer who will be conducting these trainings and share the information (CV, references etc.) related to that specific trainer. Companies will only be able to change the expert trainer during the duration of the contract with prior written consent of The KB21. When the trainer changes KB21 will have the right to terminate the contract, if it does not consent to the change of trainer. 3. Tasks to be performed by the contractor Our trainees work on exercise projects in groups of approximately 4 people. Their work is peer reviewed and reviewed by coaches. But additionally, we want it to be reviewed by Senior Software Engineering Trainers. This aims at ensuring highest standards of code quality and best practice adherence. To this end we are looking for 14 Senior Software Engineering Trainers for code reviews (Local Expert Position) who will provide in total: approximately 9 to 9.5 hours of code reviews on complex exercise projects per group of approx. 4 trainees every week as well as one-on-one-technical coaching sessions every week There will be 57 groups of trainees that require this coaching, meaning that we are expecting approximately 520 hours of coaching per week across all groups.. The coaching will be delivered by 14 coaches, with each coach responsible for approximately 4 to 5 groups. This will be done for a defined portion of the cohort period, totalling approximately 11 weeks (3 months). The total number of consultant hours is going to be 5,715 hours. Detailed task breakdown: Code reviews: Trainees use GitHub as a version control system and remote repository. When they work on exercise projects they share their code with the trainer through a pull request. Pull requests are either feature-based or they represent the coding progress done up to a certain point in time (e.g. via a dev->main PR at a certain predefined cutoff-date) The trainer then adds detailed comments to individual lines of code in the pull request through GitHub's built-in commenting functionality. Comments relate not only to errors but also to best practices and code quality criteria. Comments need to be detailed and make the recommended improvement explicit. Trainees then edit their code and ask for a re-review. This continues until comments have been addressed to the full satisfaction of the trainer in which case the trainer marks the comments as resolved. When all comments have been resolved the trainer merges the pull request. Notifications about pull requests, comments, requests to re-review etc. are triggered through GitHub's built in notification functionalities. Additionally, they can be shared on discord or any other similar communication platform that is used for coordination between the trainer and the trainees. Technical one-on-one coaching: The trainer conducts weekly one-on-one-calls with the trainees to talk through noteworthy issues identified during code reviews and to help with particularly challenging questions faced by the trainees. Trainees prepare questions for these calls about issues they are stuck on and share those questions with the trainer before the call. During the call the trainer provides ideas for how to solve the issue verbally and shares any resource-links in the chat of the call. In some cases, requests for such technical help may also be shared in between calls on discord or any similar communication platform that is used for coordination between the trainer and the trainees. 4. Tender requirements 4.1 Qualifications of the experts needed General professional experience: At least 5 years of experience working as a Software developer Specific professional experience: At least 3 years of experience working in an advanced developer role in international projects Coaching / Training experience: Experience in coaching Rwandan junior developers and experience as a trainer 4.2 Specifications of input Tasks Number of hours/ weeks Total number of hours for the assignment Code reviews for participants regarding their mistakes and their technology-skill development One-on-one technical coaching Approx. 520 hours per week 5,715 hours For the purpose of the financial bid, bidders shall calculate their price based on exactly 5,715 hours. This is the maximum estimated volume of services; KB21 Ltd. is not obliged to use the full number of hours, and payment will be made only for hours actually performed. The weekly volume of approximately 520 hours is indicative and may vary according to the needs of the assignment, within the overall maximum. 5. Requirement on the format of the tender The quote should include: A financial quote Evidence of commercial register entry A signed declaration by the company submitting the quote, confirming that none of the exclusion grounds listed in the “Eligibility criteria” section apply. Trainer CV The criteria table (can be merged with Trainer CV, for details see Criteria Table section below). Please make sure to provide a reference for each experience you mention in the criteria table. The structure of the tender must correspond to the structure of the ToR. In particular, the criteria table should be organised in accordance with the positively weighted criteria in the assessment grid (not with zero). The tender must be drawn up in English language. Criteria table Please submit a table in the format below. Use one row for each criterion, and list the name of the company / organization. The criteria table can be combined with the CV’s, as long as the matching between criteria and experience is made obvious. Criteria Experience Reference for each experience General professional experience Specific professional experience Coaching / Training experience 6. Evaluation Criteria The technical assessment is based on this technical assessment grid. An offer will be selected, if the vendor is eligible and the offer ranks the best based on the combined reached points in the technical assessment (weighted 70%) and the price assessment (weighted 30%). 7. Eligibility criteria Eligibility criteria for this tender are: Evidence of commercial register entry Exclusion grounds: The tenderer must provide a signed declaration confirming that none of the following situations apply: Criminal convictions for corruption, fraud, money laundering, or other offences affecting professional integrity; Insolvency, bankruptcy, liquidation, or similar proceedings; Serious professional misconduct affecting the ability to perform the contract; Actual or potential conflict of interest with the contracting entity or the project. 8. Submission of Quotes, relevant dates Deadline for submission of quotes is the 05th of November 2026. Please submit your quotes by uploading them to https://www.the-gym.rw/Senior-Software-Engineering-Trainer-Local-Expert Service provision is expected to start on the 09th of November 2026.

raw_text: TERMS OF REFERENCE PROCUREMENT AND SUPPLY OF VOCATIONAL TRAINING MATERIALS Procuring Entity: Rwanda National Union of the Deaf (RNUD) Tender Title: Supply and Delivery of Materials for Various Vocational Skills Tender Reference Number: RNUD1910/MUB/2026 Date of Issue: 22nd October 2026 Submission Deadline: 25th October 2026 1. Background The Rwanda National Union of the Deaf (RNUD) is an organization committed to promoting the rights, inclusion, empowerment, and socio-economic development of Deaf persons in Rwanda. The Menya Ukorane Ubuzima Bwiza (MUB) Project, funded by the European Union, aims to promote the rights and inclusion of persons with disabilities, enabling them to participate actively in society and achieve greater self-reliance and independence. The project is implemented in partnership with the See You Foundation (Netherlands) as the lead organization and RNUD and UPHLS as an implementing partner. As part of its commitment to promoting inclusion, skills development, and economic empowerment, RNUD intends to procure materials and supplies to support beneficiaries’ activities under the MUB Project. These materials will contribute to strengthening practical skills, fostering self-reliance, and expanding economic opportunities. In this regard, RNUD invites qualified, eligible, and experienced suppliers to submit quotations for the supply and delivery of vocational training materials in various fields, including tailoring and knitting, carpentry, shoemaking, soap making, hairdressing and beauty services, baking, and other related trades, as detailed in the attached list of required materials. 2. Purpose of the Tender The purpose of this tender is to identify and select a qualified supplier or suppliers capable of providing quality vocational training materials that meet RNUD's requirements and are delivered within the stipulated timeframe. 3. Scope of Supply The selected supplier(s) will be required to supply materials and equipment for various vocational skills, including but not limited to: Tailoring and garment making; Carpentry and woodworking; Shoemaking and shoe repair; Soap making; Hairdressing and beauty services; Baking and pastry making; and Other vocational training activities specified in the attached list. The detailed list of required items, including descriptions, quantities, and any applicable specifications, is attached to these Terms of Reference and forms an integral part of the tender documents. 4. Requirements for Suppliers Interested suppliers must meet the following requirements: Be legally registered and authorized to conduct business in Rwanda. Have the capacity and experience to supply the requested materials. Provide a valid Tax Identification Number (TIN) and applicable tax compliance documentation, where required. Submit a detailed financial quotation covering the items offered, unit prices, quantities, applicable taxes, and total cost. Indicate the availability of the requested items and the proposed delivery period. Provide information on the warranty or after-sales service for equipment, where applicable. Demonstrate the ability to deliver the materials to the location specified by RNUD. 5. Submission Requirements Interested suppliers are invited to submit the following documents: A signed and stamped quotation on the supplier's official letterhead; A copy of the valid business registration certificate; A copy of the supplier's TIN certificate; Applicable tax clearance or compliance documents, where required; A brief company profile or evidence of relevant experience, where available; and Any additional documentation specified in the tender announcement. 6. Evaluation and Selection Criteria Submissions will be evaluated based on the following criteria: Compliance with the administrative and eligibility requirements; Conformity of the proposed materials to the specifications provided by RNUD; Competitiveness and transparency of the quoted prices; Quality and durability of the materials; Availability of the requested items and delivery timeframe; and Supplier experience, reliability, and capacity to fulfill the order. RNUD reserves the right to select one or more suppliers, depending on the items offered, compliance with the requirements, value for money, and procurement needs. 7. Delivery Requirements The selected supplier(s) shall deliver the materials in accordance with the quantities, specifications, and delivery schedule agreed upon with RNUD. All materials must be new, of acceptable quality, fit for their intended purpose, and consistent with the approved quotation and attached specifications. Delivery shall be made to the location communicated by RNUD. The supplier(s) shall be responsible for ensuring that the materials arrive safely and in good condition. 8. Payment Terms Payment shall be made in accordance with RNUD's applicable financial and procurement procedures and the terms agreed upon with the selected supplier(s). Any applicable taxes, transport costs, and other charges must be clearly indicated in the quotation. 9. Submission Procedure and Deadline Interested suppliers should submit their complete tender documents through the submission channel indicated in the official tender communiqué. Submission deadline: 24th October 2026 at 23:59’(11:59PM) Submission address/email: infornud2010@rnud.org Submissions received after the deadline may not be considered. 10. General Conditions RNUD reserves the right to verify the information and documents submitted by bidders. Any material supplied must comply with the approved specifications and agreed quality standards. RNUD reserves the right to reject non-compliant submissions or cancel the procurement process in accordance with its applicable procurement procedures. Submission of a quotation does not guarantee contract award. All procurement decisions shall be made in accordance with RNUD's applicable procurement policies and procedures. 11. Scope of work The Supplier shall supply, deliver, and install the following, and provide commissioning support to restore full sensor functionality: Conduct a deep a detailed system inspection to diagnose the root cause of the failure and propose the most adequate solution PREVISTORM® Electric Field Sensor Motherboard, 24V , replacing the damaged unit identified in the site inspection. Associated connection cables, adapters, and consumables required for a complete, functional installation (e.g., RS232 to USB adapter cable, sensor connection cabling). On-site installation of the replacement part into the existing enclosure/mounting, reconnection to the system console, and verification of communication and readings. Basic operational training for the Organization's designated personnel on monitoring the console output and recognizing fault conditions. 2 Spare Part Specification (for Reference) The Supplier shall confirm exact part numbers and compatibility with the existing PREVISTORM® installation prior to order confirmation. Item Reference Qty Notes PREVISTORM® Electric Field Sensor Motherboard, 24V 700023 1 Primary replacement part RS232 (D-Sub 9) to USB Adapter Cable 700053 1 Console communication interface Connection cabling / accessories [Confirm with supplier] As required To match existing installation Detailed technical specifications of PREVISTORM® Electric Field Sensor Motherboard, 24V. Normative: IEC 62793:2016. CLASS A. EN 55011/22 (Radiated and Conducted) EN 61000-3-2, EN 61000-3-3 EN 61000-4-3, EN 61000-4-4, EN 61000-4-5, EN 61000-4-6, EN 61000-4-8, EN 61000-4-11 Environmental: Operating temperature: -23ºC a +50ºC. Humidity: 0% a 100%. IP Level: IP65. Construction: Operating principle: Electric Field Mill. Motor type: brushless. Material: Stainless steel and aluminium. Fixation: Direct insertion into the mast top. Weight: 1,85kg. Electric: Cabling: 20 meters multi-via cable. Contact INGESCO for other lengths and customizations. Power: Standard model: 24V±10%@500mA(max). Extended model with de-icing: 48V±10%@2.0A(max). Communications interface: Isolated RS232, 57600, 8n1, Full-duplex. Signalling outputs: 2 isolated relay outputs. Operation: Measurement range: ±100kVm-1. Resolution: 1Vm-1 (when operating at highest sensitivity). Precision: ±10Vm-1 (when operating at highest sensitivity). Data rate: 4 samples per second. Lightning detection range: up to 20km. Response time: 150ms (with data filtering disabled). Alarm levels: 4 (No alarm, Level 1, Level 2 and Level 3). Options and extras: Power supply: Consult INGESCO. Customized cable: Contact INGESCO. De-icing and heaters: Available only for the 48V model. Recommended for installation in sites where snow and frost occur. Remote console: Console with LCD display, integrated power supply, and four (4) dry relay outputs. Contact INGESCO specifying the product code “PREVISTORM® Thunderstorm Warning System MAD” Jacobus Johannes Visagie, General Manager Attachment attachment_file_541cad857646b2015510

raw_text: Project/Activity Name Heifer International Rwanda Agresso Work order: RW0000 Country: Rwanda Advertisement for Procurement Request for Quotation (RFQ) Heifer International Rwanda (HIR) is a Nonprofit and International Non-governmental Organization with the mission to alleviate hunger and poverty, while caring for the environment through sustainable agricultural practices. In collaboration with the Government of Rwanda and other relevant partners, this project has now grown to cover the whole country to become the flagship program known as “one cow per poor family”. Heifer International Rwanda projects focus on improving income and nutritional status, mobilizing farmers, and promoting local capacity through training of project participants, promoting market linkages for dairy value chain actors, improving the quality of livestock through artificial insemination services, empowering rural women, building resilience through sustainable agricultural practices, and connecting local communities to business development services. Heifer International Rwanda partners with smallholder farmers to build sustainable livelihoods by empowering them to use their own energy, ingenuity, and dreams to fuel their success out of hunger and poverty. Heifer programs mobilize communities and foster the organization of associations, cooperatives and social networks while strengthening their capacity to address development challenges. Purpose and Objective The main objective of this tender is to ensure the timely, reliable, and high-quality supply of office stationery to support Heifer International Rwanda’s daily administrative and operational activities. The selected supplier will ensure the consistent availability of essential stationery items to facilitate efficient office operations, and the achievement of Heifer’s program and business objectives.
